tools.name: xentral_agent_jobs
tools.description:
Job CRUD + single-job inspection / editing / approve on the agent-hub-labs jobs system.

QUEUE OPS:
- `list_pending` — jobs that need human attention (status: requires_intervention, waiting, ready). Use this when the user asks 'wo muss ich noch handeln' / 'welche Jobs sind offen'. Newest first. All filters (`agent`, `category`, `min_confidence`, `max_confidence`, `since`, `until`) are optional — only pass when the user explicitly asks. `agent` matches a single agent name exactly; `category` covers ALL agents in that bucket at once (e.g. 'customer_service' covers every CS-Sub-Agent — Refund-Return, Order-Management, Inquiry, …). Both can be combined.
- `create` — create a manual job (mirrors 'Neue Aufgabe erstellen'). Required: `content` (natural-language description). Optional: `title`, `agent` (from `xentral_agents` action='list'). Customer/article references are extracted automatically from `content` by the agent.
- `complete` — mark a job done. Pure status flip with optional audit `note`. Does NOT send any emails — run EmailAccount `sendEmail` via `xentral_erp_core` first if you also want to email the customer.

INSPECT A SINGLE JOB (require `job_id`):
- `get_email` — original customer email (body, subject, sender, received-at), incl. `originalRequest` envelope and attachments. Use when the user asks 'wie sah die Mail aus' / 'was hat der Kunde geschrieben'.
- `get_response` — the AI's suggested response that would be sent on approve (plus locale translations + the `info` summary).
- `get_steps` — planned tool steps with positional indices. The indices are what you pass to update_step / delete_step / insert_step.

EDIT BEFORE APPROVE (require `job_id`):
- `update_response` — overwrite the suggested response. Required: `suggested_response`.
- `update_step` — change a step's name / description / parameters / actionable. Required: `step_index` + at least one of `step_name`, `step_description`, `step_parameters`, `step_actionable`.
- `delete_step` — remove a step. Required: `step_index`.
- `insert_step` — insert a new step AFTER `step_index` (pass `-1` to append at the end). Optional: `step_name`, `step_description`, `step_parameters`, `step_actionable` (defaults: 'custom_step', 'Manuell hinzugefügter Schritt', {}, true).

EXECUTE (real side effects — confirm with user before invoking!):
- `approve` — heavyweight Approve flow: persist edits, send the reply email (Xentral/Zendesk depending on `originalTicketSource`), optionally run the planned steps against the ERP, then close. Required: `job_id`. Switches: `send_email` (default true), `close_job` (default true), `execute_steps` (default FALSE — set true only when the user explicitly wants the planned ERP actions to be performed). Edited-content overrides: `edited_email_content`, `edited_subject`, `edited_to`, `edited_cc`, `edited_bcc`. THIS IS THE ONLY ACTION THAT SENDS MAIL / TOUCHES THE ERP — never trigger it without explicit user confirmation.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

agent.description:
Agent name as exact-match string. The list of valid agent names is instance-specific — call `xentral_agents` action='list' first to see which agents are enabled in this Xentral instance.
For `list_pending`: filter jobs to ONE specific agent (e.g. 'customer_service_refund_return'). To get all agents of a bucket at once, use `category` instead.
For `create`: target agent for the new job; omit for automatic routing via the orchestrator.

category.description: For `list_pending` (optional): filter to all agents in that category at once. 'customer_service' covers every CS-Sub-Agent (Refund-Return, Order-Management, Inquiry, …). Combine with `min_confidence` to e.g. 'alle CS-Jobs mit Confidence > 0.7'.

max_confidence.description: For `list_pending` (optional). Useful to surface low-confidence cases.

since.description: For `list_pending` (optional): ISO 8601 lower bound on createdAt.

until.description: For `list_pending` (optional): ISO 8601 upper bound on createdAt.

content.description: For `create`: natural-language task description. Include order numbers, customer names, article numbers, etc. so the agent can resolve them in the ERP.

title.description: For `create` (optional): short title shown in the job inbox.

note.description: For `complete` (optional): audit note appended to the job.

suggested_response.description: For `update_response`: the new draft response that will replace `emailComparison.suggestedResponse`. Markdown / plain text / HTML — same content the FE editor produces.

step_index.description: 0-based position of a step in `plannedToolsSteps`. Required for `update_step`, `delete_step`, `insert_step`. For `insert_step` use `-1` to append at the end. Get the current indices via action='get_steps'.

step_name.description: For `update_step` (optional) and `insert_step` (optional, defaults to 'custom_step'): tool name that this step invokes on approve. Must match a Xentral ERP tool filename in `backend/thirdpartytools/xentral/` (e.g. 'create_sales_order', 'update_customer').

step_description.description: For `update_step` / `insert_step` (optional): human-readable description shown in the job UI.

step_parameters.description: For `update_step` / `insert_step` (optional): parameters passed to the tool on approve. Shape matches the tool's `execute(...)` kwargs — call action='get_steps' first to see the existing shape.

step_actionable.description: For `update_step` / `insert_step` (optional, default true). When false the step is informational and gets skipped on approve.

send_email.description: For `approve` (default true): if false the job is closed but no email is sent — useful when the user has already replied manually.

close_job.description: For `approve` (default true): if false the job stays open after the email is sent — useful for multi-step interventions where more work is expected.

execute_steps.description: For `approve` (default FALSE): if true, run every actionable step in `plannedToolsSteps` against the Xentral ERP after the email is sent. Set true only when the user explicitly wants the planned ERP actions performed.

edited_email_content.description: For `approve` (optional): HTML body that overrides the stored `suggestedResponse` for this send only. If you want the edit persisted on the job, use action='update_response' first instead.

edited_cc.description: For `approve` (optional): CC header for the outgoing email.

edited_bcc.description: For `approve` (optional): BCC header for the outgoing email.

tools.name: xentral_agents
tools.description:
For domain context, constraints and recipes: call `action='help'` first. For machine-readable agent-type metadata (semantic guidance for picking the right `cadence`): call `action='agent_types'`.

Agents available in the instance + their custom-agent calendar (when each agent runs). Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual (domain semantics, pitfalls, recipes). Pass `locale='de'` for German, otherwise English.
- `agent_types` — structured JSON catalogue of every supported `cadence` value with id, label, plain-language description, `when_required` flag and example use-cases. **Call this BEFORE `custom_agent_add` when the user describes intent in plain words** (e.g. 'a form that the supplier fills in', 'a chat bot for the helpdesk', 'daily morning briefing') — it's the canonical mapping from intent to cadence and prevents picking the wrong trigger.
- `list` — agents enabled in the instance. Use this when the user asks which agents are available, or before `xentral_agent_jobs` action='create' if you want to assign the new job to a specific agent.
- `custom_agent_list` — all custom-agent slots, optionally filtered by `cadence`. Response includes `slots`, `by_cadence`, `counts`, `total`.
- `custom_agent_schedule` — slim schedule view: per slot only `cadence`, `when`, `enabled`, `next_run_at`, `last_run_at`, `last_status`. Sorted by `next_run_at` ascending; manual/event/chat slots appear at the end with `next_run_at: null`. First choice for the question "who runs next?".
- `custom_agent_add` — create a new slot. Required: `cadence`, `when`, `agent`, `area`, `note`.
- `custom_agent_update` — change slot fields by `slot_id`. The id always changes after a successful update (it's a hash of content) — use the new id in subsequent calls.
- `custom_agent_remove` — delete the slot identified by `slot_id`.
- `custom_agent_move` — convenience for drag-drop: pass `slot_id` and one or both of `new_cadence` / `new_when`.
- `erp_event` — manage the ERP webhook behind a `cadence='event'` slot (requires `slot_id`). `erp_event_op`: `get` (default) | `activate` (needs `event`) | `deactivate`. **Creating an event slot subscribes nothing.** The scheduler skips the `event` cadence by design, so a slot stays inert until you activate it here — do not report an event agent as live before `get` shows `erp_event_active: true`.

## Agent-Type-Guide (which `cadence` to pick)
Cadence is NOT just a scheduler enum — it's the **agent trigger type**. Each value below is a different kind of agent. Pick by user intent, not by 'how often it runs'. When in doubt, call `action='agent_types'` for the full JSON catalogue.

USER-TRIGGERED — these have no time, `when` stays empty:
  `manual`  Quick task — user clicks 'run now' in the Schedule view. Ad-hoc job on demand.
  `form`    Form agent — you send a recipient a LINK, they open it, FILL IN a structured form, agent processes the submission. **Pick this when the user wants someone to enter data and have the agent react.** Examples: return registration, supplier onboarding questionnaire, master-data update from customer, product-data capture.
  `chat`    Chat-bot — user TYPES INTO A CHAT surface, agent replies in turn. Interactive Q&A. NOT for structured data entry — use `form` for that. Examples: internal FAQ-bot, helpdesk-bot.

SYSTEM-TRIGGERED — `when` carries a match expression, NOT a time:
  `email`   Inbox agent — fires on every incoming mail that matches. `when` = match hint (e.g. `subject:invoice`).
  `event`   ERP event — fires on a data change (new sales-order, delivery status flip). `when` = AsyncAPI event name. Adding the slot does NOT subscribe it: finish with `action='erp_event'`, `erp_event_op='activate'`, or the agent silently never runs.

TIME-BASED — `when` is required and follows the cadence's format:
  `appointment`  one-off ISO date/time; disables itself after the run.
  `daily`        `HH:MM`           (e.g. `09:00`)
  `weekly`       `MON|TUE|WED|THU|FRI|SAT|SUN HH:MM`  (e.g. `MON 08:00`)
  `monthly`      `<1-31>. HH:MM`   (e.g. `1. 09:00`)
  `quarterly`    `Q1|Q2|Q3|Q4`     (first day of the quarter, 09:00)
  `yearly`       `DD.MM. [HH:MM]`  (e.g. `01.07. 09:00`)

All times are Europe/Berlin local.

## Full configuration surface (everything the UI exposes is also a tool param)
Every field the user can edit in the Agent-Konfiguration UI can be set via `custom_agent_add` or `custom_agent_update`. Don't tell the user 'you have to do this in the UI' — pass the right param.

Core (all cadences):
  `prompt`        Anweisungen / system prompt. Plain text, can include numbered steps. Same field as the 'Anweisungen'-Box in the UI.
  `tools`         array of **MCP-tool slugs** the agent may use at runtime. Pass the FULL slug exactly as it appears in this server's `tools/list` — do NOT abbreviate. Pickable values (any with `annotations.agent_pickable=true`):
                    `xentral_copilot` (ERP-Co-Pilot — read & write Belege)
                    `xentral_agent_jobs` (Jobs für andere Agenten)
                    `xentral_decisions` (Entscheidungen-Liste)
                    `xentral_agents` (Agenten anlegen/ändern)
                    `xentral_schedules` (Cron-Schedules)
                    `xentral_business_model` (Plan-Seiten lesen/schreiben)
                    `xentral_groups` (Agenten gruppieren)
                    `xentral_dashboards` (Dashboards anlegen/editieren)
                    `xentral_kpi` (KPIs verwalten)
                    `xentral_reports` (Analytics-Reports)
                    `xentral_pdf_templates` (PDF-Vorlagen anpassen)
                    `xentral_connections` (Integrationen prüfen)
                    `xentral_erp_core` (ERP-Daten & -Konfiguration — Records lesen/schreiben, Settings-Entities wie Warehouse/TaxRate/PaymentMethod)
                    `xentral_fileshare` (Files lesen/ablegen — CSVs, Verträge, Reports)
                    `xentral_knowledge_base` (Faustregeln & gelerntes Wissen)
                  Common recipes:
                  - Form-Agent, der eine CSV erzeugt → `['xentral_copilot', 'xentral_fileshare']` (Co-Pilot zieht die Daten aus dem ERP, Fileshare legt die CSV ab).
                  - Chat-Agent für Kundenservice-Anfragen → `['xentral_copilot', 'xentral_erp_core', 'xentral_knowledge_base']`.
                  - Briefing-Agent für Dashboard-Werte → `['xentral_copilot', 'xentral_kpi', 'xentral_decisions']`.
                  Slugs that do NOT match a registered MCP tool are silently dropped at run time; the slot's job timeline will list them under `missing`.
  `model`         OpenAI model id, e.g. `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`. Default applies if omitted.
  `temperature`   creativity 0.0 – 2.0 (UI 'Kreativität'-slider). Typical values: 0.2 for strict factual flows, 0.7 for balanced (UI default), 1.0+ for creative drafting.

Cadence-specific (`form` slots):
  `form_meta` = {
    audience: 'external' | 'internal'   # extern = public link, intern = login required
    fields: [                            # ordered list, max 50
      { id, label, type, placeholder?, required? },
      ...
    ]
  }
  field types: text, textarea, number, email, url, select, checkbox, date, file
  → For a 6-field product-data form: pass 6 entries in `fields` in one call. The slot is fully configured after `custom_agent_add` returns — no UI step needed.

Cadence-specific (`chat` slots):
  `chat_meta` = { header_name, header_color, subtitle, welcome, bubble_teaser, position: 'bottom-left'|'bottom-right', embed_enabled: bool, starters: [string, ...] (max 12) }

Cadence-specific (`email` slots):
  `email_meta` = { auto_reply: bool, match_criteria: string }
  `when` for email cadence carries the inbox filter expression, NOT a time.

## Embedding slots inside a dashboard
Slots are not only reachable as standalone surfaces — every `form` / `chat` / `manual` slot can ALSO be embedded inline in a dashboard via the `xentral_dashboards` widget catalogue's `Agent` widget. Add an `Agent`-widget to the dashboard with `config.agents[]` referencing the slot's `agent_name`; the widget renders form-shape / chat-shape / button-shape automatically based on the referenced slot's `cadence`. So the answer to "can I add a form to my dashboard?" is YES — create the form slot here, then attach it via `xentral_dashboards`. See the dashboards help (`action='help'`) section 'Interactive — let the user trigger an agent from the dashboard' for the widget-config shape.

## Naming custom agents (the `agent` field)
When `custom_agent_add` creates a NEW agent (the slot defines it via `prompt`, not just schedules an existing one), the `agent` field is the display title shown in the sidebar, schedule view and slot list. Use a short, capitalised, human-readable label in the user's language — e.g. `Produktdaten erfassen`, `Lieferanten-Onboarding`, `Tägliches Verkaufs-Briefing`. NEVER pass `snake_case`, `kebab-case`, lowercase slugs or technical ids here (e.g. NOT `product_data_capture`, NOT `daily-sales-briefing`). The UI renders the string verbatim. Only use slug form when assigning a slot to a BUILT-IN agent listed by `action='list'` — then the slug must match exactly.

## Anti-patterns to avoid
- Don't create a `manual` slot when the user wants a form — use `form` + `form_meta.fields`.
- Don't pass `agent='product_data_capture'`-style slugs when creating a custom agent — use a proper title like `Produktdaten erfassen`.
- Don't tell the user 'fields must be configured in the UI' — pass `form_meta={fields:[…]}` directly on `custom_agent_add`.
- Don't drop a CSV into Fileshare and call it a 'form template' — Fileshare is file storage, not a UI. For real recipient-fillable forms, create a `form` cadence agent with `form_meta`.
- Don't conflate `chat` (interactive Q&A) with `form` (structured one-shot submission).

## What is NOT (yet) configurable via this tool
- Knowledge attachments (UI: 'Wissen — Dateien direkt als Wissen anhängen'). Use `xentral_fileshare` to upload + `xentral_knowledge_base` to register facts. Slot-level knowledge-file binding is a UI-only feature today.
- Form share-link / form color (UI: 'Teilen-Link', 'Farbe' on form agents). The link is auto-generated; color is a UI-only convenience and not currently persisted in `form_meta`.

Slot data lives in its own storage namespace `custom_agents/<license>/agents.*` and is decoupled from the business model.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

cadence.description: Slot cadence — required for `custom_agent_add`, optional filter for `custom_agent_list`.

erp_event_op.description: For action='erp_event' (requires `slot_id`): manage the ERP webhook subscription behind a `cadence='event'` agent slot. Saving the slot alone subscribes NOTHING — the scheduler skips the `event` cadence by design, so until `activate` runs the slot is inert and the agent never fires. `get` reports the current state; `activate` (needs `event`) registers upstream; `deactivate` removes the subscription. Default `get`.

event.description: For action='erp_event', erp_event_op='activate': the event-type id in the active ERP core's own vocabulary — for Xentral e.g. 'com.xentral.salesOrder.created.v1'. Enumerate the valid ids with `xentral_erp_core action='events'`; they are per-installation and per-version, so never guess — an unknown id is refused at activation. Note that events fired at document CREATION may arrive before the document's line items exist; pick the event that matches the state your agent needs to read.

core_id.description: For action='erp_event': which of the instance's ACTIVATED cores to register the webhook against, and whose event catalogue applies. Omit for the primary. Ids come from `xentral_erp_core action='list'`.

connection_id.description: For action='erp_event', erp_event_op='activate': which ERP connection to subscribe through. Omit for the tenant's default. Recorded on the subscription so a later teardown targets the same system.

when.description: Time expression matching the cadence's format (see description).

agent.description: For slots that route to a BUILT-IN agent (one returned by `action='list'`): pass the existing `agent_name` slug verbatim, e.g. `customer_service_order_management`. For slots that DEFINE a new custom agent (i.e. you also pass `prompt` and the slot itself is the agent): this is the human-readable display title shown in the sidebar and schedule view — use a short, capitalised label in the user's language, e.g. `Produktdaten erfassen`, `Lieferanten-Onboarding`, `Rücksendung anmelden`. NEVER use snake_case, kebab-case or lowercase slugs for custom-agent labels (the UI shows the string verbatim, so `product_data_capture` looks like a developer leak).

note.description: Short description of what runs in this slot.

internal_comment.description: Why this agent slot was scheduled — set by the onboarding coach on add/update. One to three sentences referencing the business-model or research signal that motivated this routine. Shown on hover in the onboarding tab.

prompt.description: Anweisungen / system prompt for the agent. Plain text (can include numbered steps). Same field as the 'Anweisungen'-Box in the UI. Use for `custom_agent_add` / `custom_agent_update`.

tools.description: Full MCP-tool slugs the agent may use at run time. Pass the slugs exactly as they appear in `tools/list` (any tool with `annotations.agent_pickable=true`). Examples: `xentral_copilot`, `xentral_fileshare`, `xentral_decisions`, `xentral_kpi`, `xentral_dashboards`, `xentral_knowledge_base`, `xentral_erp_core`. NEVER pass short bundle ids like `copilot` or `fileshare` — those do not resolve at run time and the slot will run with no tools bound.

model.description: OpenAI model id (e.g. 'gpt-5.1', 'gpt-4o', 'gpt-4o-mini'). Defaults to the instance default if omitted.

temperature.description: Kreativität slider value (0.0 strict to 2.0 wild). UI default is 0.7. Use ~0.2 for factual/transactional flows, 0.7 for balanced, 1.0+ for creative drafting.

form_meta.description: Configuration for `cadence='form'` slots — defines what the recipient sees and fills in. Shape: { audience: 'external'|'internal', fields: [{ id, label, type, placeholder?, required? }, ...] }. Field types: text, textarea, number, email, url, select, checkbox, date, file. Max 50 fields. Pass the full field list on `custom_agent_add` — the slot is configured in one call.

audience.description: external = public link (Captcha + Rate-Limit), internal = login required.

chat_meta.description: Configuration for `cadence='chat'` slots. Shape: { header_name, header_color, subtitle, welcome, bubble_teaser, position: 'bottom-left'|'bottom-right', embed_enabled: bool, starters: [string, ...] (max 12) }.

email_meta.description: Configuration for `cadence='email'` slots. Shape: { auto_reply: bool, match_criteria: string }. The `when` field for email cadence carries the inbox filter expression (e.g. 'subject:invoice'), NOT a time.

tools.name: xentral_business_model
tools.description:
For domain context, section semantics, profile enum values and recipes: call `action='help'` first.

Manage the instance's business plan (Notion-style markdown editor) and the top-level Unternehmensprofil. Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German, otherwise English.
- `read` — without `slug`: list all sections with metadata (title, group, exists, lastModified). With `slug`: return that one section's full markdown plus metadata.
- `write` — write or append to one section. `mode='replace'` (default) overwrites the entire section markdown. `mode='append'` adds to the end of the existing content. The frontend editor live-updates via the filesystem watcher — no manual refresh needed. Always `read` the section first before a `replace` so you don't clobber existing structure.
- `apply_template` — apply a starter template that pre-fills sections with a focused skeleton. Without `template`: returns the list of available templates so you can present them to the user. With `template`: writes the skeletons to disk. `overwrite=false` (default) preserves any section the user already edited; pass `true` to wipe-and-replace.
- `profile_get` — read the Unternehmensprofil (6-dimension classification: Geschäftsmodell, Vertrieb, Fulfillment, Automatisierung, Größe, Komplexität) plus a compact summary string.
- `profile_set` — set one or more profile dimensions. By default (`merge=true`) only the explicitly passed fields are updated; the rest stay as they were. Pass an empty value to clear a field. The 6 fields are strict enums — invalid values are rejected. The profile lives as the regular `profile` section in the plan, so a markdown `read`/`write` still works, but `profile_set` is the only path that enforces the enum contract.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

slug.description: Section slug. For `read`: omit to list all sections. For `write`: required.

markdown.description: For `write`: the markdown content. For `mode=replace` the full new content; for `mode=append` the snippet to tack on.

mode.description: For `write`: how to apply the markdown. Default `replace`.

template.description: For `apply_template`: template id. Omit to list available templates instead of applying.

overwrite.description: For `apply_template`: if true, wipe existing section markdown and replace with the template skeleton. If false (default), only fill sections that are still empty.

sales_channels.description: For `profile_set` (optional): Vertriebskanäle. Mehrfachauswahl erlaubt — z. B. `['E-Commerce', 'Marktplätze']`.

size.description: For `profile_set` (optional): Unternehmensgröße. Small=2–10 Mio · Mid=10–50 Mio · Upper=50–100 Mio.

merge.description: For `profile_set`: if true (default), only set fields are updated. If false, the entire profile is replaced — unset fields become null.

tools.name: xentral_connections
tools.description:
Connector catalog + live instance connection state + official Xentral API/Webhook documentation pointers.

Connections is the **only** instance-data feature without per-instance storage on our side — the actual connection state (which Shopify shop, which DHL account) lives in Xentral itself. The library (Shopify, Shopware, DHL, Stripe, …) lives as JSON under ``backend/connections/library/data/`` so the list can be extended without a code deploy.

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `list_library` — full library (97+ providers) plus the category-label map. Use this first when the user asks "welche Schnittstellen unterstützt Xentral?".
- `get_card` — one provider's full record (id, name, category, description, source URL on marketplace.xentral.com). Requires `card_id` (e.g. `shopify`, `dhl`, `datev`).
- `list_active` — **live** state from Xentral: which connectors the instance has active, account count, account details. 5-min cache; pass `refresh=true` to bypass after the user just connected something.
- `docs` — pointers to the official REST API spec, Webhook spec, and 3PL/generic integration patterns. Pass `topic='rest_api'|'webhooks'|'3pl'` for a single section, or omit for the whole map. Use this when the user asks how to build their own integration.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for `list_active` when the JWT doesn't already carry the license_id; ignored for the library/doc actions.

topic.description: For `docs`: which documentation section to return. Omit for the full map.

locale.description: UI locale, 'de' or 'en'. Unknown values fall back to 'en'. Affects the localised description in the catalog payload.

refresh.description: For `list_active`: bypass the 5-min cache and fetch fresh from Xentral. Set after a connect/disconnect.

tools.name: xentral_copilot
tools.description:
Primary tool for any question that touches ERP data — call this FIRST. The Co-Pilot can search and create customers, suppliers, sales orders, products, invoices, delivery notes, returns and more, plus run analytics (revenue, margin, top-N, trends, period summaries). Pass the user's question through largely unchanged. Only fall back to your own reasoning when the Co-Pilot returns no data.

If you don't already know the target instance, call `xentral_instances` action='instances' first.

ANALYTICS-CO-PILOT FALLBACK — Wenn die Antwort des Tools mit dem Satz „Pass auf, leider ist der Analytics-Co-Pilot gerade nicht erreichbar …" beginnt, ist das Reporting-Add-on aktuell nicht verfügbar. Gib diese Meldung dem User wörtlich weiter (sie enthält bereits den Hinweis auf das Customer-Success-Team) und biete an, die Frage stattdessen mit den übrigen ERP-Tools so weit möglich zu beantworten.

message.description: What you want the Xentral Co-Pilot to do, in natural language.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance. Get one from `xentral_instances`. Required unless the JWT already carries a license_id.

conversation_id.description: Optional. Pass the conversation_id returned from a previous call to keep multi-turn context.

tools.name: xentral_dashboards
tools.description:
Dashboards — library reads + per-instance CRUD. Built-in cards ship as YAML in the repo; instances are instance-owned copies the user has materialised.

Library actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German, otherwise English.
- `list_library` — discover the built-in dashboard cards
- `get_card` — full card (title, description, icon, category)
- `check` — dry-run the config self-check on a `widgets` + `layout` draft WITHOUT saving; returns `{ok, summary, findings}`. Run this before `update_instance` to catch config footguns (wrong keys, dangling / orphan layout refs, empty widgets).

Instance actions (instance-scoped, write):
- `list_instances` — all custom dashboards the instance has created
- `read_instance` — full envelope (widgets, layout, audit fields)
- `create_instance` — copy a built-in card into the instance store; a unique slug is generated server-side
- `update_instance` — patch title / description / icon / category / enabled / widgets / layout (only supplied fields change)
- `delete_instance` — remove a custom dashboard from the instance store

`create_instance` / `update_instance` responses carry an advisory `_findings` array when the saved config has issues (never blocks the save) — read it and fix, or `check` the draft first.

Cache refresh (chart widgets only):
- `refresh_widget` — re-run a single chart widget's underlying SQL and update its cache (Redis for 'cached' mode, S3 for 'snapshot' mode). Requires `slug` + `widget_id`. Use after an upstream ETL so a snapshot-mode chart picks up the new numbers without a human click.
- `refresh_all_widgets` — same, but for every chart widget in a dashboard. Skips widgets without a saved Xentral report.

Always discover with `list_library` or `list_instances` first. For the widget-type catalogue (TableTabs, KpiGrid, HeroStats, Charts, AgentWidget, …) and the supported `TableTabs.view` values, call `action='help'`.

**Custom-entity tables — the one explicit consumption path from the foundation layer**: a `TableTabs` widget with `view='entity'` + `entity_key='<key>'` is the ONLY place where a raw `entity_key` from `xentral_erp_core` `list` is consumed by another tool. Use this for embedding tables of entities that have no first-class view (e.g. cost centres, instance-extended custom entities). Standard entities (`customers`, `products`, `supplier_invoices`, `inbox`, …) go through their named `view` values — do NOT route them through `view='entity'`.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for any instance-scoped action.

template_id.description: Dashboard card slug (e.g. 'customer_service'). Required for `get_card` and `create_instance`.

slug.description: Per-instance dashboard slug returned by `create_instance`/`list_instances`. Required for `read_instance`, `update_instance`, `delete_instance`, `refresh_widget`, `refresh_all_widgets`.

widget_id.description: Widget id within the dashboard (e.g. `w-linechart-abc123`). Required for `refresh_widget`. Use `read_instance` to discover the available widget ids.

name.description: Display name for the new instance (defaults to the template's title).

enabled.description: Toggle the dashboard on/off in the sidebar. For `create_instance` the default is `true` (dashboard appears immediately); pass `false` to stage a hidden draft. For `update_instance` the field is left unchanged when omitted.

widgets.description:
Ordered list of widget instances. Each item is `{id, type, config}` where `type` is a value from the platform widget catalogue (call `action='help'` to see the full list with config shapes — `GreetingCard`, `HeroStats`, `KpiGrid`, `TableTabs`, `AttentionBlock`, `Agent`, `LineChart`/`BarChart`/etc., `HtmlBox`). Do NOT invent new types — only catalogue names render.
- `HtmlBox` reads its markup from `config.htmlContent` (NOT `html` — a wrong key renders an empty box). The value is a plain HTML string or a `{de, en}` object.
- For embedding ERP-record tables, use `TableTabs` (see help for the `view` enum, including `view='entity'` + `entity_key` driven by `xentral_erp_core list`).
- For embedding a form / chat / button surface that triggers a custom agent (e.g. "quick supplier create form" on the dashboard), use the `Agent` widget with `config.agents[]` referencing the slot by `agent_name`. The widget shape (form / chat / button) is derived from the referenced slot's `cadence` — so a form-slot renders as a form right inside the dashboard tile.

layout.description:
Layout definition. Two dialects:
- `{type:'split', main:[...], side:[...]}` — sidebar + main column; each is a list of rows (a widget id or an array of ids for an equal-width side-by-side row).
- `{type:'grid', rows:[...]}` — the flexible grid. Each row is `{cols, cells}`: `cols` is the column template (numbers = relative weights, e.g. [8,4] = 2:1, [4,4,4] = thirds, [12] = full-width; or {px:n} / {fr:n} objects for fixed / flexible tracks) and `cells[i]` holds the widget(s) for column i. Write EACH cell as an array of ids — `[['a'], ['b','c']]` — a single-widget column is `['id']`, a stacked column is `['id1','id2']`. (A bare string is tolerated but the array form is the convention every built-in uses — stay consistent.)
To add a ROW: append `{cols:[1], cells:[['<id>']]}` to `rows`. To add a COLUMN to a row: push a weight onto its `cols` and a cell onto its `cells`. Read the current layout with `read_instance` first, edit `rows`, then send the whole `layout` back — only supplied fields change. The grid is a superset of split, so split dashboards keep working unchanged.

internal_comment.description: Why this dashboard was chosen — set by the onboarding coach at install time. One to three sentences referencing the business-model or research signal that motivated the pick. Shown on hover in the onboarding tab.

locale.description: UI locale, 'de' or 'en'. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_datasets
tools.description:
The customer's own managed data — organised as SETS OF TABLES ('lite datatables'), isolated per tenant in a dedicated Postgres. A DataSet groups several tables (like a Supabase project). Use this to create sets and tables, evolve columns, and read/write rows. NOT ERP master data (customers/orders/products/invoices) — for those use `xentral_erp_core`.

Tables are REAL typed Postgres relations (text/integer/number/boolean/date/datetime/uuid/json/select + reference=FK), so you can also run read-only SQL with the `query` action.

Datasets have a lifecycle: you build a DRAFT, a human activates it. As an agent you may create/edit and ARCHIVE only your own drafts — you cannot hard-delete or purge, and cannot touch an active dataset.

Actions: `list_sets`, `create_set`, `describe_set`, `archive_set`, `create_table`, `describe_table`, `archive_table`, `add_column`, `rename_column`, `drop_column`, `rows`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `query`, `rows_bulk`, `import_session`, `import_analyze`, `import`, `import_status`, `import_sessions`, `session_cleanup`, `help`. Call `help` for the full parameter guide.

Got a CSV from the customer? Have them upload it via `xentral_fileshare`, then `import_analyze` it and show the warnings BEFORE importing — a structurally shifted file parses perfectly and loads into the wrong columns.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance. Defaults to the auth-context instance.

dataset.description: Set name (the DataSet). Letters, digits, underscores; starts with a letter.

table.description: Table name inside the set (for table/column/row actions).

tables.description: For create_set: initial tables, each {name, label?, columns?[]}.

references.description: For a reference column: target table name in the same set.

unique.description: Enforce a UNIQUE constraint on this column.

references.description: For a reference column: target table name in the same set.

unique.description: Enforce a UNIQUE constraint on this column.

references.description: For a reference column: the target table name in the same set (adds a real FK to its id).

unique.description: For add_column: enforce a UNIQUE constraint on the column.

not_null.description: For set_not_null: whether the column is required (NOT NULL).

default.description: For set_default: the column's DEFAULT value (omit / null to drop the default).

pk.description: For create_table: primary-key strategy (default 'auto' = bigint identity; 'uuid'; 'speaking' = r_1…).

file_key.description: For import_analyze/import: key of a CSV uploaded via xentral_fileshare(action='upload').

limit_rows.description: For import: PROBE RUN — load only this many rows, into `<table>_probe`. Use 5 first, show the rows, get confirmation, then repeat without this to load the whole file.

session_id.description: Import session id from import_session. Pass it on every import so session_cleanup can undo the whole thing later; required for import_status/session_cleanup.

ignore_warnings.description: For import: proceed despite a blocking structure warning (e.g. column_shift). Only set this after showing the warning to the user and getting a deliberate decision — the data will land in the wrong columns.

column_names.description: For rows_bulk: the column order the value arrays follow.

rows.description: For rows_bulk: rows as arrays of values, positionally matching `column_names`. Max 500 per call.

search.description: For rows (optional): free-text search over text columns.

sort.description: For rows (optional): column name, prefix '-' for descending.

limit.description: Page size. For `rows`: default 50, capped at 200. For `query`: default 100, capped at 1000.

page.description: For `query` (optional): 1-based page number; pages of `limit` rows over the result set. The result carries `page`/`size`/`has_more`.

sql.description: For `query`: one read-only SQL statement, run scoped to the DataSet's schema (SELECT / information_schema; writes are rejected). Table names are the `sql_name` from describe_table.

tools.name: xentral_decisions
tools.description:
For the full manual (categories, what belongs / doesn't belong, good decision-text patterns, lifecycle states): call `action='help'` first — pass `locale='de'` for German.

Manage the decisions list ('Entscheidungen') — the cross-area surface where humans and agents see every running operational item, what the agents are waiting for, who owns each decision, and what the agent's suggested next step is. Stored as a Notion-style markdown checklist with extended sub-bullet metadata (owner, status, money, due date, linked job ids, suggested actions). The Decisions board frontend renders the same data.

WHAT BELONGS HERE:
- Human-only setup steps (Logo hochladen, IBAN bestätigen, Training mit Vertrieb)
- Strategic / awareness items the CEO or team-lead must see ('Forderungen über 30 Tage', 'Lieferant XY ausgefallen')
- One-off action items that get checked off when done
- Reminders for a person — the value is the nudge, not the data

WHAT DOES NOT BELONG (use the right tool instead):
- Business entities (customers, orders, products, invoices) → `xentral_copilot`
- Agent jobs or running decisions → `xentral_agent_jobs`, not this list
- Knowledge, routing rules, recurring patterns the agent should recall → `xentral_knowledge_base`
- Long-form text or documents → `xentral_business_model` action='write'
- Anything an agent can do automatically — automate it, don't park it as a manual decision
- Sensitive data (passwords, tokens, full IBANs) — the list is plain markdown and visible to all instance users

Tasks are bucketed by `category`. Six categories:
- `onboarding` — Go-Live preparations (Logo, IBAN, training, …)
- `dashboard` — strategic / cross-instance items (CEO board)
- `customer_service` — CS-team backlog
- `procurement` — Einkauf-team backlog
- `logistics` — Logistik-team backlog
- `finance` — Finanz-team backlog

WRITING GOOD DECISION TEXT (for `add`):
- One decision per item — split 'X und Y' into two `add` calls.
- Start with an emoji for the dashboard icon: 🔥 critical, ⚠ warning/risk, 📦 logistics, ⏱ deadline, € financial.
- Bold the headline, em-dash, then a 1-line meta with concrete numbers. Example: '🔥 **Forderungen über 30 Tage offen** — 14 Kunden · 4 in juristischer Prüfung'.
- Single line, no nested checklists, no multi-paragraph text.
- Use stable wording — `complete`/`remove` match fuzzy on `text`, so throwaway phrasings break later updates.
- ALWAYS `list` the target `category` before `add` to avoid duplicates — the list is shared across all agents and users.

FIELD = LENGTH (a decision is a scannable card, not a document).
Only `description` may be long and multi-paragraph — it is the ONLY field rendered as multi-line Markdown/HTML, in the card's expandable body. Every other field is a single plain-text line the layout truncates. Put a daily briefing, a multi-point analysis, run results etc. in `description`; keep the rest tight. Over-budget fields are REJECTED — fix the call, don't retry the same text. Budgets:
- `text` (headline): ≤ 160 chars, single line, no line breaks.
- `value` (right figure): ≤ 24 chars, e.g. '84 k €'.
- `label` (caption under value): ≤ 48 chars.
- `question` (agent-asks callout): ≤ 600 chars.
- `description` (the long body): ≤ 6000 chars, Markdown/HTML.
So a daily-briefing decision is: a short `text` headline (e.g. '📊 **Daily Briefing Lena & Tim** — Umsatz €0, 3 offene Bestellungen') with ALL the numbered findings in `description`.

Actions:
- `list` — open decisions. `category` filters one bucket. `only_open=false` returns done decisions too. The response always includes `byCategory` with per-bucket counts.
- `add` — append a new open decision. `text` required. `category` decides which bucket; defaults to `onboarding`.
- `complete` — mark the first decision matching `text` as done. Fuzzy substring match (case-insensitive). `category` restricts the search if multiple decisions could match.
- `reopen` — flip a done decision back to open.
- `remove` — delete the first decision matching `text`. Permanent, no undo — prefer `complete` unless the decision was created in error.

action.description: Which operation to perform. `assign` sets owner, `set_status` sets lifecycle status, `link_job` / `unlink_job` attach/detach job ids, `list_by_job` returns all decisions linked to a given job.

owner.description: For `add` / `update` / `assign`: a REAL Xentral user to own the decision — pass a global_user_id, an email, or the user's name; it is resolved server-side to the canonical id plus a display-name snapshot. An unknown value is rejected (no fantasy names). Empty / omitted on `assign`/`update` = unassign (the decision becomes open again). Tasks with no owner are 'open'.

status.description: For `add` / `update` / `set_status`: lifecycle status. Distinct from `tone` (urgency color) and the done-checkbox. Drives the four status groups in the Decisions board.

amount_cents.description: Machine-readable amount in cents — used to aggregate '€ blocked' across all decisions. `value` remains the human display string ('4.280,00 €').

linked_entity.description: ERP entity this decision is about, format 'type:id' (e.g. 'sales_order:4421'). Used by the UI to make the decision title click-through to the entity detail.

due_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC due-date. Separate from createdAt — drives SLA escalation and the 'older than 24h' filter.

linked_jobs.description: For `add` / `update`: the full set of job ids linked to this decision (overwrites). Prefer `link_job`/`unlink_job` for incremental changes.

description.description: For `add` / `update`: the LONG-FORM body of the decision — the ONLY field rendered as multi-line Markdown/HTML (in the card's expandable body). This is where a daily briefing, multi-point findings, run results, numbered lists etc. belong — NOT in `text`. Use Markdown (headings, **bold**, bullet lists, links). ≤ 6000 chars.

question.description: For `add` / `update`: structured 'agent asks' question, rendered as a callout in the decision card. Markdown allowed. Keep it focused (≤ 600 chars); move supporting detail into `description`.

source.description: Origin of this decision — e.g. 'agent_run:abc123', 'email', 'webhook', 'manual'. Audit aid.

category.description: For `list`: filter to one bucket. For `add`: target bucket (default `onboarding`). For `complete`/`reopen`/`remove`: optional restriction for fuzzy matching.

text.description: For `add`: the new decision HEADLINE — a single scannable line, ≤ 160 chars, no line breaks. Start with an emoji (🔥 ⚠ 📦 ⏱ €) for the dashboard icon, bold the headline, then a 1-line meta after an em-dash. Long write-ups (briefings, multi-point findings) go in `description`, NOT here — over-long text is rejected. For `complete`/`reopen`/`remove`: substring of the decision to match (case-insensitive).

new_text.description: For `update`: the replacement HEADLINE (same rules / ≤ 160 chars as `text`). Use it when a number in the headline changes. If omitted, the headline stays; pass `description` to (re)write the long body.

value.description: For `add` (optional, dashboard widget field): right-side primary FIGURE on the card, e.g. '84 k €'. A short number/label (≤ 24 chars), not a sentence.

label.description: For `add` (optional, dashboard widget field): right-side secondary caption under `value` (≤ 48 chars). Longer text goes in `description`.

impact.description: For `add` (optional): 1–10. Drives the Dashboard's 'Sortiert nach Wirkung' ordering. Reserve high values — if everything is 10, nothing is.

tone.description: For `add` (optional): visual color of the dashboard card. `warn` (default, red), `info` (neutral), `positive` (green).

only_open.description: For `list`: return only open decisions (default true).

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

locale.description: UI locale for the `help` action — 'de' or 'en'. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_erp_core
tools.description:
Operate the ERP directly — day-to-day back-office work AND configuration, through one tool: find, read, create, update and delete business records (customers, products, sales orders, invoices, suppliers, …) as well as configuration/settings records (cost centers, warehouses, payment methods, custom entities, …), and trigger business actions and process steps (ship an order, book an invoice, …).

Whatever the user wants done IN the ERP, this is the tool: `list` shows which entities exist on this instance, `describe` shows an entity's fields, filters and available actions, then `records`/`get`/`create`/`update`/`delete`/`run` work on live data. Responses are the core's own payloads returned verbatim (the same implementation a workflow `business-entity` node resolves).

NOT this tool: dashboards (`xentral_dashboards`), KPIs (`xentral_kpi`), building agents (`xentral_agents`), free-form analytical questions (`xentral_copilot`).

Metadata:
- `help` — Markdown guide (`locale='de'` for German), followed by the active core's own **playbook** when it ships one: the entities, actions, statuses and filters that matter for everyday work, and — crucially — which declared capabilities that core cannot execute. Read it before planning a workflow; it saves a `list` plus a round of speculative `describe` calls. Pass `core` to read another activated core's playbook.
- `list` — full catalogue `{source, categories, entities:[…]}` plus `primaryCore` (the instance's active core), `secondaryCores` (activated browse-only cores) and `activeCore` (the core this payload was composed for).
- `describe` — one entity's fields (`key`): typed, with writability (`access`/`creatable`/`updatable`) and queryability (`filterable`/`sortable`/`searchable`, plus select `options`); a flat `query` contract lists the exact keys `records` filters/sorts/searches on; plus `operations`, `actions` and `processSteps` — each action / step command with its `command` param schema, destructive/bulk flags and verified status, ready to feed `run`.
- `events` — which events this ERP core can PUSH, live from the instance: `{events:[{id, group, label, schema}], core:{supportsEvents,…}}`. READ `schema` BEFORE writing a trigger reference: it is the JSON Schema of the whole delivery, so an event field sits at `schema.properties.body.properties.<name>` and is read as `{{ trigger.body.body.<name> }}` — `trigger.body` is the envelope and carries only `type` and `body`. The id field is named per entity (`salesOrderId`, `deliveryNoteId`) and cannot be guessed. `schema: null`, or a `body` with `additionalProperties: true` and no `properties`, means the fields are NOT described — not that there are none. This is the only way to enumerate them; the ids are per-installation and per-version, so never reuse one you have not seen in this response. Feed an `id` verbatim as the `event` when activating an ERP-event trigger (`xentral_workflows action='erp_event'`). A core that cannot push events answers `supportsEvents: false` with an empty list — a valid answer, not a failure.

Platform API reference (Xentral's published OpenAPI documents — the same data for every instance, no core needed; for building a customizing integration or checking what the HTTP API offers beyond the core. To read or change data on THIS instance, use the entity actions above instead):
- `api_search` — find endpoints by keyword (`query`, optionally `spec`/`method`, `per_page` caps the rows). Without `query`: the catalogue of available specs.
- `api_endpoint` — one operation in full, incl. parameters and request body: `op` (an `operation_id` from `api_search`) or `path` (+ `method`).
- `api_schema` — a component schema by name (`query`), `$ref`s inlined two levels; a fragment lists the matching names.

Data (need `key`; returns `{status, body}` verbatim):
- `records` — list records (`page`, `per_page`, `filters`, `sort`). `sort` is a field key from `describe`'s `query.sortable`, prefix `-` for descending (e.g. `-createdAt` for newest first).
- `get` — one record (`handle`).
- `create` — new record (`body`).
- `update` — change a record (`handle` + `body`).
- `delete` — remove a record (`handle`).
- `run` — run an action / process step (`op` = an action key or a process-step command key from `describe`, never the group key; target via `handle` or `ids`; `command` per the entry's schema). Writes/actions hit the live ERP — a rejected op returns the core's status + reason.

Bulk import (many records via a Fileshare journal — see the ERP bulk-import guide):
- `bulk_template` — envelope + how to build payloads for `key`.
- `bulk_validate` — dryRun-check a journal (`import_id`); no ERP writes.
- `bulk_run` — create records under a wall-clock `time_budget_s` (default 45s, under the ~60s prod wall): it measures the real per-item time and processes as many as fit, so heavy payloads auto-yield fewer per call. Re-invoke until remaining=0 (`chunk_size` ≤ 200 optional hard cap, `concurrency` ≤ 8, `retry_failed`). Progress is persisted as it goes, so it resumes and never runs one long request.
- `bulk_status` — progress snapshot of a journal (`import_id`), no writes.
- `bulk_stop` — durably stop a run (`import_id`): every later `bulk_run` no-ops until one is called with `resume=true`. Stop takes effect at the next chunk boundary.
Create OR update: set the journal `meta.op` to 'create' (default) or 'update'; update items add a `handle` (the record id) and a payload of just the fields to change. Same validate/run/stop/resume flow.

Multi-core: `list` returns `primaryCore`, `secondaryCores` (activated cores) and `connections` (`{core_id: [{id, label, primary}]}` for cores with own credentials). Pass `core=<id>` on any action to target an activated core without switching the instance (reads AND writes — activation is the gate), and `connection=<id>` to target one of that core's connections instead of its primary (e.g. a second Odoo database). Omit both for the instance's primary core + primary connection.

key.description: Entity key (from action='list'), e.g. 'SalesOrder'. Required for describe and all data actions.

handle.description: Record id. Required for get/update/delete; also the default target for `run` when `ids` is omitted.

body.description: Record fields for create/update, in the entity's own (core) shape — see action='describe'.

op.description: Key to run (from action='describe'): an `actions[].key` or a `processSteps[].commands[].key` — NOT the step group key. Required for action='run'. For `api_endpoint` it is instead an OpenAPI `operation_id` from `api_search`.

command.description: Command payload for `run`, per the entry's `command` schema from action='describe' (`required` names the mandatory properties). Omit when the entry declares no command.

per_page.description: Page size for `records` (default 25); for `api_search` the max number of rows (default 50, hard cap 200).

filters.description: List filters for `records`: [{key, op, value}] (op defaults to 'equals', and to 'contains' on the consolidated 'search' key).

sort.description: Sort key for `records` — a field from `describe`'s `query.sortable`. Prefix `-` for descending, e.g. `-createdAt` for newest first. The core validates the key.

query.description: API-reference search text: keywords for `api_search` (all tokens must match), or a component-schema name / name fragment for `api_schema`.

spec.description: Optional API-reference spec id (from `api_search` without a query), e.g. 'main' or 'documents'. Omit to look in all of them.

path.description: `api_endpoint`: the endpoint path exactly as the spec lists it, e.g. '/api/v1/salesOrders' — an alternative to `op`.

method.description: HTTP method for the API reference: narrows `api_search`, and picks the operation for `api_endpoint` when a path has several.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required when the JWT does not already carry a license_id.

core.description: Optional entity-core id to scope the call to — the primary or one of `secondaryCores` from action='list'. Applies to ALL actions (reads and writes); a non-activated core is rejected. Omit to use the instance's active core.

connection.description: Optional connection id (from `list`'s `connections` map) to scope the call to one of the core's own connections — e.g. a second Odoo database — instead of its primary. Applies to all actions; must belong to the scoped core. Omit to use the core's primary connection.

import_id.description: Bulk actions: the journal's importId — also the Fileshare tag `import:<importId>` the journal is stored under. Required for `bulk_validate` / `bulk_run`.

chunk_size.description: `bulk_run`: max records to process this call (default 50, hard cap 200). Each call is one bounded chunk — re-invoke until remaining=0.

concurrency.description: Bulk actions: concurrent upstream calls (default 4, max 8). The tenant serializes writes, so higher does not help.

retry_failed.description: `bulk_run`: also re-attempt items already marked `failed` (default false — only `pending`/`valid` are processed).

resume.description: `bulk_run`: clear a prior `bulk_stop` and continue. Without it, a stopped import stays stopped and every `bulk_run` no-ops (so a looping caller halts too).

time_budget_s.description: `bulk_run`: wall-clock budget per call (default 45s, safely under the ~60s prod wall). The call measures the real per-item time and stops before the budget is exceeded, so heavy payloads auto-yield fewer records per call. Raise it where there is no tight timeout to do more per call.

locale.description: UI locale; passed as `Accept-Language` for localised labels. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_feedback
tools.description:
Record a user's verdict on a tool action the agent just performed (a thumbs up/down with a category and optional comment). Recording only — never touches ERP data.

Ask **at most once per task**, and only after a successful high-value action (create · update · send · workflow/automation creation · PDF/template creation · destructive/high-impact). Never after reads or routine look-ups; never re-ask if ignored; skip for automated runs.

Actions:
- `help` — this manual.
- `record` — store one feedback event. Requires `source_tool`, `source_action`, `rating`, `category`. High-signal feedback (negative, or bug/wrong_result/confusing_ux, or `request_report=true`) is relayed to the team Slack; positive/neutral is stored quietly.

Pass references (entity ids), not document/email contents, and don't paraphrase sensitive data into `comment`.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance the feedback belongs to. Required when the JWT doesn't already carry the license_id.

source_tool.description: For `record`: the tool whose action is being rated, e.g. `xentral_erp_core`.

entity_type.description: For `record`: optional type of the entity the action touched, e.g. `correspondence`, `sales_order`.

entity_id.description: For `record`: optional id of the touched entity. Pass the reference, not its contents.

category.description: For `record`: what kind of feedback this is.

comment.description: For `record`: optional free-text in the user's own words. Truncated to 2000 chars. Don't include sensitive document or email contents.

request_report.description: For `record`: set true only when the user explicitly asks to report/escalate this. Forces a team notification.

tools.name: xentral_fileshare
tools.description:
Per-instance working-file storage (Datenaustausch / Fileshare) — uploaded CSVs, price lists, contracts, generated reports, and anything else the team or agents drop here. NOT ERP master data: for customers / orders / products / invoices use `xentral_copilot` or the dedicated ERP tools. These are transient documents that act as input or output for agent workflows.

NOT a form-builder. If the user wants someone to fill in data and have an agent react to the submission, that is a `cadence='form'` agent — use `xentral_agents` (action='agent_types') and then `custom_agent_add` with `cadence='form'`. Dropping a CSV template here is only the right call when the user wants to download an empty file, fill it in offline, and re-upload it (rare).

Actions:
- `list` — newest-first list of files for the instance, with metadata only (no contents). Optional `source` / `tags` / `limit` filters.
- `metadata` — full metadata for one file by `file_key`.
- `read` — read the file's contents. Text-MIME files return inline UTF-8; binary files return base64 if small (<100 KB). A text file too big to return whole is read in WINDOWS: pass `offset` (1-based line) and `limit` (lines, default 200) and continue from the reported `to_line`. The response always says whether more follows — never report a window as the file.
- `find` — search a text file line by line without loading it: `pattern` (substring, or `regex=true`), optional `ignore_case`, `context` (lines around each hit, max 5), `max_hits` (default 50). Returns line numbers you can feed back as `read`'s `offset`. This is how you locate something in a file too large to read.
- `upload` — create a new file. Pass exactly one of `content` (plain text body) or `content_b64` (base64-encoded binary), plus `filename` (required), `mime_type` / `description` / `tags` (optional).
- `update` — change a stored TEXT file in place, keeping its `file_key`: `content` replaces the whole body, `old_string` + `new_string` patches exactly one occurrence (ambiguous or missing anchors are refused, never guessed). Irreversible — there is no version history. Allowed without ceremony only on files YOU uploaded; an inbound email attachment is never overwritten; for anything else prefer `upload` under a new name, and pass `confirmed=true` only when the user explicitly asked to overwrite that file.
- `delete` — remove one file by `file_key`.
- `help` — return the Fileshare agent guide (when, how, constraints, common flows). Pass `locale='de'` for German.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance. Defaults to the auth-context instance.

file_key.description: UUID of the file. Required for `metadata`, `read`, `find`, `delete`.

filename.description: Original filename. Required for `upload` (drives MIME-type guess + display name).

content.description: Text body. For `upload`: the new file's content (CSVs, JSON, text, code — not images/PDFs). For `update`: the replacement body, only for a file small enough that you have read all of it.

old_string.description: For `update` (patch form): the exact text to replace. Must occur EXACTLY once — include surrounding lines until it is unique.

new_string.description: For `update` (patch form): what replaces `old_string`. May be empty.

confirmed.description: For `update` on a file you did not upload: set only after the user explicitly asked to overwrite THIS file and you told them it cannot be undone. Never set it on your own initiative.

content_b64.description: Base64-encoded binary content for `upload`. Use this for PDFs, images, ZIPs.

mime_type.description: Optional MIME-type for `upload` (e.g. 'text/csv', 'application/pdf'). Guessed from filename if omitted.

description.description: Optional human-readable note for `upload` (e.g. 'Q4 price list from supplier X').

limit.description: For `list`: max entries (default 50, max 500). For a windowed `read` (i.e. with `offset`): how many lines (default 200, max 2000).

offset.description: For `read` (optional): 1-based line to start at. Passing it turns `read` into a window — the only way to read a text file that is over the inline cap.

pattern.description: For `find` (required): substring to search for, or a regular expression when `regex=true`.

context.description: For `find` (optional): lines of context before/after each hit (0-5, default 0).

max_hits.description: For `find` (optional): stop after this many hits (default 50, max 200). The response says when it stopped early.

tools.name: xentral_groups
tools.description:
Groups — instance-owned bundles that tag Business Skills, Agenten, Workflows, Connections, PDF-Vorlagen, Studio-Apps and Dashboards under one named umbrella (e.g. '3PL', 'Belege Steuerberater'). Use when the user wants to plan / structure a coherent process directly instead of going through the onboarding-coach. Members keep their identity — a group is just a view and a tag.

Call `action='help'` first for the full domain guide (member roles, ownership semantics, conflict resolution modes, recipes).

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown guide. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `list` / `read` — overview or full envelope.
- `create` / `update` / `delete` — manage the group.
- `add_member` / `remove_member` — wire items in or out. Needs `member_type` + `ref_id`; optional `mode` resolves cross-group role conflicts (see `help`).

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for any instance-scoped action when the JWT does not already carry a license_id.

group_id.description: Stable group id returned by `create` / `list`. Required for `read`, `update`, `delete`, `add_member`, `remove_member`.

name.description: Display name. Required on `create`; on `update` only changes the name when supplied. Short and concrete reads best (e.g. '3PL', 'Export Steuerberater').

icon.description: Symbol key for the group tile. Defaults to 'folder' on create. Free-text; the frontend maps known keys to icons.

description.description: One- or two-sentence explanation of what this group covers — read by the user in the detail view and by future agent calls.

status.description: Top-level rollout state. Auto-derived on read unless manually pinned to 'paused'. Only relevant for `update`.

internal_comment.description: Why this group exists — rationale set by the agent or user. Free-text, shown on hover; distinct from `description` which is the public summary.

member_type.description: Kind of item being added to / removed from the group. Required for `add_member` / `remove_member`.

ref_id.description: Canonical id of the underlying item: `block_id` for blocks, agent slug for agents, connection id for connections, template `name` for PDF templates, workflow `id` for workflows, app slug for studio apps, dashboard slug for dashboards. Required for `add_member` / `remove_member`.

mode.description: How to resolve a cross-group role conflict on `add_member`. `auto` (default) picks owner when the item is unclaimed and otherwise returns a conflict descriptor. `claim` takes ownership from another group; `shared` puts the item into joint ownership; `reference` adds a read-only mention.

locale.description: Locale for the `help` manual. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_instances
tools.description:
List the agent-hub-labs instances (Xentral instances) the calling user has access to, and manage per-instance access consents.

Every other Xentral tool requires an active consent for the target instance before it will execute. Consent is per-user x per-instance and persists until revoked. On first contact with an unconfirmed instance, the server pushes a confirmation banner to the user's open agent.xentral.com tab; the user grants access by clicking "Erlauben" there. Calling this tool with `action="confirm_access"` fires that same banner on demand.

Actions:
- `list` (default) -- directory of available instances
- `list_consents` -- which instances the user has consented to
- `confirm_access` (requires `instance_id`) -- fire the consent banner so the user can grant access
- `revoke_access` (requires `instance_id`) -- drop a consent
- `revoke_all_access` -- drop every consent for the caller

action.description: What to do. Defaults to `list` for backward compatibility.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance. Required for `confirm_access` and `revoke_access`.

tools.name: xentral_integrations
tools.description:
External agent-tool catalog (Gmail, Slack, Google Drive, …) connectable via managed OAuth, plus live per-instance connection state. This is the **new Integrations Hub** (`/app/integrations`) — distinct from `xentral_connections`, which covers the old Xentral-marketplace connectors (Shopify, DHL, Datev, …).

Connections + OAuth tokens live with the managed connection service, not on our side — we never store credentials. Connections are keyed per (instance, user).

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `list_catalog` — full catalog of connectable integrations plus the category-label map and 'popular' ids. Filter with `category` for sub-questions. Use first when the user asks "which external tools can the agent connect?".
- `get_card` — one integration's card metadata (id, name, category, description, auth scheme, connectable). Actions/triggers are not in the card (loaded live in the hub dialog). Requires `card_id` via `template_id` (e.g. `gmail`, `slack`).
- `list_actions` — one toolkit's **live, curated** action + trigger schemas (same set the hub dialog shows). Requires `template_id`. Returns empty when integrations are not configured.
- `list_connected` — **live** connection state: which integrations the current (instance, user) has authorized. Returns empty when integrations are not configured.
- `search_catalog` — search **every** toolkit our provider offers (a superset of the curated catalog) by name or slug via `query`. Each match flags `in_catalog`/`connectable`. Use this to find the exact slug before `request_interest` for something not in `list_catalog`.
- `request_interest` — record an instance's interest in an integration that can't be connected yet, via `template_id` (a catalog id OR any real toolkit name/slug); optional `note`. A curated 'Coming soon' card joins its waitlist; a real-but-uncurated toolkit is logged as demand. An already-connectable one is rejected (just connect it); something no real toolkit matches is rejected (don't guess — `search_catalog` first). The instance is always recorded; the requester's email is included when it's a real person, else attributed to the automated agent.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for `list_connected` when the JWT doesn't already carry the license_id; ignored for the catalog actions.

template_id.description: Integration id / slug (e.g. `gmail`, `slack`, `googledrive`). Required for `get_card`, `list_actions` and `request_interest` (for the latter, a real toolkit name also works — it's resolved to a slug).

query.description: For `search_catalog`: a toolkit name or slug to search the full provider catalog for. Ignored by other actions.

note.description: For `request_interest`: optional free-text use case for the integration (max 500 chars). Ignored by other actions.

category.description: For `list_catalog`: filter to one category slug. Omit for the full catalog.

locale.description: UI locale, 'de' or 'en'. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_inventory
tools.description:
Single-call discovery of every named, openable thing the user has in their instance — Workflows, Dashboards, KPIs, custom Agents, PDF templates, Connections and Studio apps.

Use this when the user names something to open ('öffne Bene Formular', 'gehe in CEO-Cockpit zum bearbeiten', 'show me KPI Umsatz') and you don't yet know which category that name belongs to. One inventory call returns everything; match the user's name (fuzzy / case-insensitive) against the items, then call `xentral_user_context` action=`open_entity` with the matched `entity_type` and `id`. Faster and more reliable than probing the per-domain list tools one by one.

Each item has shape `{id, name, entity_type, ...}` where `entity_type` is exactly the string `open_entity` expects (`workflow`, `dashboard`, `kpi`, `custom_agent`, `pdf_template`, `integration`, `studio_app`). A `counts` block reports how many items per category.

Action:
- `list` (default) — return the full inventory.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

tools.name: xentral_kpi
tools.description:
Instance-scoped KPI store. One stable identifier per metric, multilingual labels, unit, value-type, optional group, plus an append-only history of every value ever written. KPI cards across the product read from here so the same number never lives in two places.

Lifecycle: `init` registers a KPI once. `set_value` writes a new value (the previous one is archived to history automatically). Prefer `set_active=false` for KPIs that shouldn't appear in default lists but whose history you want to keep. Use `delete` only when the KPI was created in error and its historical data is worthless — it wipes envelope + every history shard.

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German, otherwise English.
- `list` — all KPIs for the instance. Filter by `group` or `active_only=false`.
- `get` — full envelope for one KPI. Pass `include_history=N` to attach the last N rows.
- `init` — register a new KPI. Requires `key`, `labels`, `value_type`. `unit` is optional (leave empty for dimensionless tallies). Optional `group`, `initial_value`. Fails if `key` already exists.
- `set_value` — write a new value to an existing KPI. Requires `key`, `value`. Optional `as_of` (ISO-8601 UTC, default now), `note` (locale → descriptive sub-line), `tone` (`positive | warn | negative`). Fails if KPI is missing or inactive.
- `set_active` — toggle the visibility flag. Requires `key`, `active`.
- `set_track_history` — turn persistent history-recording on/off for a live/cached KPI. Requires `key`, `enabled` (bool). When enabled, every value change observed by the live resolver is appended to the same monthly history shards that push KPIs use (deduped: a row is only written when the resolved value differs from the previous history entry, so unchanged reads don't spam). Off by default — live KPIs otherwise only expose the current value with no timeline. Reject on push KPIs (they always write history on `set_value`).
- `history` — return historical values, oldest first. Optional `last_n`. Works for push KPIs (always populated) and live/cached KPIs that have `track_history=true` enabled. Returns an empty list when nothing has been recorded yet.
- `delete` — hard-delete envelope + history + index entry. Requires `key`.

ALWAYS call `init` before `set_value` on a new metric. Don't rename keys — KPI cards pin to the key.

**Trends for live/cached KPIs.** By default a derived KPI (`value_source` in `live`/`cached`) only stores the current value — every read recomputes it from the linked Xentral report. If you need a sparkline or a queryable timeline (e.g. to show 'open orders over the last 30 days'), call `set_track_history` with `enabled=true`. From that point on, every distinct value the resolver observes is appended to the history shards, and `history` / `get include_history=N` start returning rows. Toggling off stops new appends but keeps everything already recorded.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for any instance-scoped action.

labels.description: Locale → display label, e.g. {"de": "Offene Retouren", "en": "Open returns"}. 'en' is required.

value.description: New value (number or string). Required for `set_value`.

note.description: Optional descriptive sub-line per locale, e.g. {"de": "40 offen", "en": "40 open"}. Used on `init` (as initial_note) and `set_value`.

tone.description: Optional tone hint that colours the value in the UI. Set per write so agents can re-decide every time.

as_of.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the value refers to. Defaults to now.

enabled.description: Required for `set_track_history`. When true, the live resolver starts appending every value change of a live/cached KPI to the history shards (deduped against the most recent entry). When false, recording stops but past entries remain readable.

active_only.description: Filter `list` to active KPIs only. Default true.

include_history.description: When set on `get`, attaches the last N history rows.

internal_comment.description: Why this KPI was registered — set by the onboarding coach at init time. Should name the consuming dashboard/widget (e.g. 'Wird im Hero des ceo_overview-Dashboards gezeigt'). Shown on hover in the onboarding tab.

locale.description: UI locale for `help`. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_knowledge_base
tools.description:
Knowledge Base CRUD — the instance's evolving knowledge base, agent routing rules, organisation facts, automations and response templates. Use this whenever the user shares a fact worth remembering ('merk dir, X ist immer dringlich') or asks about what's stored ('wie wird X gerouted', 'was wissen wir über Y', 'welche Automatisierungen laufen').

NOT for API mechanics. Endpoints, field names, HTTP verbs and 'this does not work' claims are refused on write: they belong in the entity core (as a capability or a `wish`), where they are versioned and tested, not in a tenant store where they never expire. Entries stored before that rule carry `unverified_mechanics` on read — treat those as hearsay and re-check against the core.

Actions:
- `read` — without `entry_id`: paged list filtered by `entry_types` / `agent`. With `entry_id`: full single entry (only routing/automation rows are looked up by id; knowledge-scope ids are PG-side).
- `write` — create a new entry. `entry_type` must match the data: `knowledge` (Q&A), `routing` (email→agent), `organization` (company info), `automation` (mini-agent prompt + tools), `template` (response template). Knowledge / organization / template go to AI Platform PG; routing / automation stay in SQLite. `agent` defaults to '*' (instance-global). For automation: `tools_list` are the tool names the mini-agent can call; `triggers` are events that fire it.
- `update` — edit fields by `entry_id`. Pass only fields you want to change. The id shape decides storage: numeric → PG (only `question`, `answer`, `entry_type` editable); UUID → SQLite (all fields).
- `delete` — by `entry_id`. Same id-shape routing as `update`.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

entry_id.description: For `read` (optional): fetch one entry. For `update` / `delete` (required): id of the entry.

entry_types.description: For `read` (optional): filter to one or more types.

agent.description: For `read` (optional): filter to one agent's scope. For `write` (optional, default '*'): agent the entry is scoped to. For `update` (optional): change scope (SQLite rows only).

entry_type.description: For `write` (required): which kind of entry. For `update` (optional): change the type.

question.description: For `write` (required): title / question / trigger description. For `update` (optional): change it.

answer.description: For `write` (required): answer / target / agent prompt. For `update` (optional): change it.

tools_list.description: Automation only — tool names the mini-agent may call.

tools.name: xentral_onboarding_coach
tools.description:
Xentral Onboarding-Methode — lädt die schlanke Onboarding-Disziplin für eine neue Instanz. KEIN Skript, keine festen Phasen: Geschäft konkret verstehen, konkret vorschlagen, einen Plan entwerfen, den der Nutzer selbst ausführt (du planst, der Nutzer führt aus).

**Wann aufrufen**: Sobald der User Einrichtungs-Intent signalisiert — Begriffe wie ``Xentral einrichten``, ``Onboarding starten``, ``zu Xentral wechseln``, ``Geschäftsmodell erstellen``, ``Hilf mir bei der Erst-Einrichtung``. Auch wenn der User allgemein um Hilfe beim Aufsetzen bittet und die Instanz noch leer ist.

Actions:
- ``start`` (default) — lädt die Methode (kurzes Markdown). Du wendest sie in deiner eigenen Advisor-Stimme an — nicht rezitieren, kein Intake-Menü, überspring was der User schon gesagt hat. Akzeptiert ``locale='de'|'en'``.
- ``help`` — kurzer Überblick (was die Methode ist, wann starten). Aufrufen wenn der User fragt was du anbieten kannst, OHNE das Onboarding zu starten.
- ``version_check`` — vergleicht ``current_version`` gegen die Server-Version. Returns ``{server_version, is_outdated, download_url, changelog_since, user_message_de}``.

Für die eigentliche Umsetzung nutzt du die anderen ``xentral_*`` Tools (business_model, agents, dashboards, connections, pdf_templates, onboarding_plan).

action.description: Which operation to perform. Default: start.

current_version.description: Embedded skill version (e.g. '1.0.0') for ``action='version_check'``. Read it from the ``Version X.Y.Z`` line at the top of the skill body. Omit / pass empty when the running skill predates versioning — the server then always reports outdated.

tools.name: xentral_onboarding_plan
tools.description:
Per-instance onboarding roadmap: which templates (blocks, agents, dashboards, connections, pdf) the instance should set up, plus human-tasks and test-runs. Each item's status is **resolved live** against the matching backend (block instances, agent slots, …) — no drift between the plan and the real state.

Two distinct concerns:
- **Catalog mapping** — items reference templates from the 5 feature catalogs via `kind` (`block`/`agent`/`dashboard`/`connection`/`pdf`) + `template_id`. When an instance for that template exists, the resolver flips status from `planned` → `active` automatically.
- **Manual items** — `human_task` (logo, IBAN, training) and `test_run` (verification scenarios) have no template; they wait on the user, status flips via `mark_done`.

ALWAYS call `action='help'` first to get the full standard (coverage, sequencing, parallelism, test-orders). Without the guide you'll produce a sloppy plan.

**Client-side regenerate flow (PREFERRED when an LLM is driving this tool):** Use `get_context` → reason locally → `propose_items` in small chunks. This avoids the long blocking call of `generate` and keeps each tool round-trip fast. Use `generate` only in headless / scheduled contexts where no client LLM is reasoning over the response.

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown standard for what a good onboarding plan looks like. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `read` — resolved plan: envelope + items annotated with live `status` and `instance_id` + summary roll-up. Use this every turn before adding more — items may have transitioned to `active` since your last call.
