- `get_context` — snapshot for the client-side flow: `{business_model, libraries, existing, allow_list}`. Returns everything needed to propose a fresh plan without a server- side LLM call. `allow_list` lists the legal `card_id` slugs per kind — only those slugs survive validation in `propose_items`.
- `propose_items` — append a batch of items (chunks of 5–10 keep the argument payload small). Server validates each item against the library (drops hallucinated `card_id`s), checks `source_kind`/`source_card_id` against the catalog (blanks invalid attribution, keeps item), and enforces Stufe-2 (`human_task` titles must match the source card's declared `human_inputs`). Reports drops so the LLM can self-correct. Set `replace_first=true` on the FIRST chunk when regenerating from scratch — wipes the plan, then appends.
- `add_item` — append a single item. Required: `kind`, `phase`, `title`. `template_id` only for non-manual kinds. `metadata` carries kind-specific extras (e.g. `min_count` + `description` for `test_run`). Unlike `propose_items` this is unvalidated — use `propose_items` whenever possible.
- `remove_item` — drop an item by `item_id`.
- `dismiss_item` — user-override: "don't need this". Item stays in the plan but the resolver returns `status=dismissed`.
- `mark_done` — user-override: "completed". Only meaningful for `human_task` / `test_run` (template-backed items get `active` automatically once an instance exists).
- `reopen_item` — clear the user override so the live resolver takes over again.
- `set_test_status` — Prüfprotokoll auf einem `test_run`-Item schreiben. Required: `item_id`, `test_status` (one of `not_checked|passed|failed|blocked`). Optional: `notes` (free-text), `linked_order_ids` (list of Xentral SO IDs the user actually placed for this permutation), `failure_reason` (only meaningful when `test_status='failed'`). Writes into `metadata.test_status` + `metadata.tested_at` + the other audit fields. Orthogonal to `mark_done` / `dismiss_item` — those gate whether the user cares about the item at all; this one records the prüflauf-outcome.
- `discard` — wipe the entire plan. Use before a full regenerate when you want a truly clean slate (or pass `replace_first=true` to `propose_items` instead).
- `generate` — SERVER-side LLM regenerate from BP + catalogs. Long-running (20–90s) — only use in headless / scheduled contexts. For interactive use prefer `get_context` + `propose_items`. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for all actions except `help`.

group_id.description: Plan a group instead of the instance-wide plan. Pass the group id (from `xentral_groups action='list'`, e.g. `3pl-eb066b28`) and the item lands in that group's plan (`group-<id>`) so it shows up in the group's Fortschritt card. Omit for the instance-wide `main` plan. Supported by read / add_item / remove_item / dismiss_item / mark_done / reopen_item / set_test_status / discard — NOT by propose_items / generate / get_context.

item_id.description: Plan-item id. Required for remove_item / dismiss_item / mark_done / reopen_item.

kind.description: For `add_item`: which catalog this item ties to. `human_task` for user-only items (logo, IBAN), `test_run` for go-live verification scenarios.

phase.description: Sequencing bucket. Order is fixed (see help). Phases 1-3 block; 4-6 may run parallel; 7 last.

card_id.description: Library card slug for non-manual kinds (e.g. `batch_picking`, `daily-finance-briefing`, `shopify`). Discover via the matching `xentral_<feature> action='list_library'`.

title.description: Display label shown in the plan UI.

reason.description: Why this item is suggested. MUST point back to a concrete BP field — e.g. "BP business_model=D2C + sales_channels=[E-Commerce]". Vague reasons lower priority.

items.description: For `propose_items`: list of item proposals to validate + persist. Each entry mirrors the `add_item` fields. Keep chunks small (5–10 items) so the argument payload stays under MCP transport limits — call `propose_items` multiple times for larger plans.

card_id.description: Card slug from the matching library (see `allow_list` from `get_context`).

reason.description: Must reference a concrete BP field, e.g. 'BP business_model=D2C'.

source_kind.description: For human_task / test_run / extension: which library area causes this item.

source_card_id.description: Slug of the source library card. Hallucinated slugs are blanked server-side (item kept).

replace_first.description: For `propose_items`: when true, wipe the plan before appending this batch. Set on the FIRST chunk of a fresh regenerate; omit on subsequent chunks so they append.

test_status.description: For `set_test_status`: the prüflauf-outcome to record on a `test_run` item. `not_checked` resets the audit fields back to untested.

notes.description: For `set_test_status`: optional free-text notes from the user (e.g. 'Carrier-Routing hat statt DHL Express einfach DHL Standard gewählt').

linked_order_ids.description: For `set_test_status`: Xentral sales-order IDs the user actually placed for this permutation. Stored as audit trail.

failure_reason.description: For `set_test_status` with `test_status='failed'`: short structured reason. Cleared automatically when the status transitions out of `failed`.

tools.name: xentral_pdf_templates
tools.description:
Vague or compliance-sensitive request (e.g. 'invoice for authorities', 'in all languages')? Call `action='survey'` first. If `create` returns `status='needs_clarification'`, ask the user those questions before creating — do not guess a compliance profile. For industry-specific rules (food = batch + MHD, B2C = always show alternate shipping address, etc.), engine semantics and pre-flight checks: call `action='help'` first. Manage PDF-Vorlagen (Lieferschein, Rechnung, Auftragsbestaetigung, Angebot, generic letter, eigene Custom-Vorlagen). Reuses the same storage as the in-app Templates UI — anything created or updated via this tool shows up in the user's library, anything deleted is removed. Actions: - `help` → Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German, otherwise English. - `survey` → read-only inventory of what the instance ALREADY has: which document types, languages and compliance tags exist across their templates (+ `intent='invoice'` lists spec e-invoice formats NOT yet present). Plus an optional demand-side usage analysis (see `analyze`). Nothing is written. Use before creating on a vague request. Add `analyze=true` (+ optional `window_months`, default 12) to also get a `usage` block — what the instance's REAL documents needed (languages, countries, currency, derived locale/translations), sourced via the Co-Pilot with an explicit `basis`/`confidence`. New instances with no history degrade to company-config/defaults, never a guess. - `list` → built-in + instance-custom templates as JSON summary - `get` → full template (html, css, example_data, schema, ...) - `check` → read-only hygiene report for ONE template (name required): empty-printing/untranslated variables (per language), unformatted date/amount fields (missing | date / | money), missing assets, an uploaded-but-unused font, number/date locale sanity, e-invoice tag without a configured policy, structural gaps. No render, no writes — safe to run anytime. Returns findings by severity. Pass `live=true` (optionally `sample_doc_id`) to ALSO render a real Beleg and judge the actual output (ISO dates, identifiers absent from the page). - `render` → render the PDF. `output='image'` returns PNG page previews you can SEE (use it to verify layout after visual edits); `output='url'`/'metadata'/'base64' give the PDF, which the model cannot view. - `create` → new custom template (name + title + html required) - `update` → patch existing custom template On create/update, `global_fields` lists the top-level `example_data` keys that are ISSUER-GLOBAL — constant across every document the instance issues (e.g. `['company']`). ONLY those fall back into a REAL document when the live payload omits them; everything else in example_data is preview-only. Omit it (or pass `[]`) and nothing falls back — so a build-time sample number/date/recipient can never print on a customer's PDF. - `delete` → remove custom template (built-ins cannot be deleted) - `set_translation` → merge UI strings for ONE language (`lang` + `translations={key: value}`). Strings render as `{{ L.key }}`; values may be strings, nested dicts (L.sec.x) or lists of pairs. Mirrors the sidebar's Übersetzungen table. - `set_debug_capture` → turn the ephemeral payload capture on/off for this template (`enabled`, default true). Persistent per template, independent of any public share. Everything the editor's 'Letzte Payload'-box does is available here. - `last_payload` → the most recent data dict that was rendered (debug aid). Needs capture enabled (see `set_debug_capture`); captured from the in-editor live preview OR a public-share call. Ephemeral (Redis, ~10 min, latest only); shows source (internal/GET/POST), doc id, render_ok/error. - `clear_payload` → delete the captured payload immediately (the flag stays as-is). Use after inspecting sensitive data. - `list_infoboxes` → the template's placeable text blocks - `set_infobox` → create/update ONE box by `infobox_key` (`placement` = intro_top|outro_bottom|footer_all|header_all, `content`/`box_title` = {lang: text}, `enabled`). Box content may use Jinja ({{ data.* }}). Validate-or-reject with rollback. - `delete_infobox` → remove ONE box by `infobox_key` EFFICIENCY (each call is a round-trip — pick the SMALLEST tool): - Smallest-tool order: `set_style` (font/column tokens) → `set_block` (one region, e.g. footer/items) → `update` with css ONLY (html untouched) → full `update` of html only as the last resort. Re-sending the whole template on every tweak is the main reason edits feel slow. - Verify with `render` + `output='metadata'` — it only confirms the template still renders (returns {filename, size_bytes}). Use `output='url'` (a visual render) ONLY when the change is visual and you must check the optics. NEVER `output='base64'` to 'look' — it streams 50-150KB through the context for nothing. - Batch related edits, THEN render once — not after every micro-step. - Do NOT `get` a template you just wrote; you already know its content. TECH STACK (relevant for HTML/CSS you generate): - Templating engine: **Jinja2 3.x** with `ChainableUndefined` (so `data.foo.bar` returns Undefined silently if `foo` is missing — no need to guard every chain, but use `| default(...)` for values you actually format). - PDF renderer: HTML templates render via **Gotenberg/Chromium** by default (fast). The service falls back to **WeasyPrint** ONLY for the *tagged* variants — PDF/UA-1 and the PDF/A-*a levels (e.g. pdf/a-3a) — and for templates using a custom `@font-face`. PDF/A-*b (incl. pdf/a-3b ZUGFeRD/Factur-X) stays on **Gotenberg/Chromium**; the PDF/A container conversion runs downstream via LibreOffice, so such files carry a LibreOffice 'Producer' — that is expected, NOT a WeasyPrint render. Build your CSS against the engine the variant actually uses. A4 + margins + per-page headers/footers come from `_base/base.css` via `@page` and work on BOTH engines. Do NOT add `@page` in your CSS. - Rules that hold on BOTH engines: * No JavaScript — pure HTML/CSS rendering * Flexbox supported, CSS Grid supported * A footer/header on EVERY page → ALWAYS `@page` margin boxes (`@bottom-left/center/right`), NEVER `position: fixed/sticky`, and NEVER `position: running()` / `content: element()` (WeasyPrint-only syntax, ignored by the default renderer) * `font-family` falls back to DejaVu/Helvetica in container; avoid `@font-face` (no internet in render context) * Use `mm` / `pt` for print dimensions, `em`/`px` for typography * Tables: `border-collapse: collapse`, `table-layout: fixed` with `` widths is most reliable * For tabular numbers use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` IMAGES & LOGOS: NEVER paste a base64 `data:` URI into `html`/`css`. Add the image once via `set_asset('logo', )` and reference it as `{{ assets.logo }}`. Inline base64 bloats the template so every later get/update/render round-trips a large blob through the model context; assets are stored separately and keep edits fast. When creating, write `{{ assets.logo }}` in the HTML and supply the image via a follow-up `set_asset` call. - Accessibility: the PDF/UA fallback emits **tagged PDF (PDF/UA-1)** when the template uses semantic HTML. Therefore: exactly one `

`, proper heading hierarchy, `` on table headers, `
` for postal addresses, `alt=""` for decorative images. - Money formatting: V3 sends amounts as STRINGS ("249.00000000"). Parse with `| float`, then `| format`, then `| replace('.', ',')` for German notation. VAT breakdown: use Jinja2 `groupby` over `lineItems` by `effectiveTaxRate` with `namespace(s=0.0)` to sum. DATA SCHEMA (Xentral V3 with `?include=all`): - data.documentNumber, data.documentDate, data.customerNumber - data.documentAddress = {name, street, zipCode, city, country} - data.effectiveAddresses.{soldTo,shipTo} = same shape - data.lineItems[] with .number, .name, .description, .quantity, .unit, .effectiveTaxRate, .price.net.amount (string), .lineItemRevenue.net.amount (string) - data.totals.net.amount, data.totals.gross.amount (strings) - data.financials.tax.taxRates ({standard:19, reduced:7}) - data.financials.paymentTerms.paymentTargetDays (invoices) - data.payment.{iban,bic,bankName} (invoices, instance-side) - data.company.{name, address, vatId, taxId, ceo, letterheadText, officeLines[], bankLines[], identityLines[], legalLines[]} — sender/footer info, NOT in V3 response. Declare `global_fields=['company']` so it falls back from example_data on REAL documents (without that, missing company fields print empty). HOW TO BUILD A NEW TEMPLATE — two steps. Think STRUCTURE first, then LOOK. STEP 1 — CLASSIFY the document and clone a structure starter: - Line-item document (invoice, order, delivery note, offer, credit note — anything with a positions table) -> clone `document_blank`. - Free-form letter (cover letter, reminder, notice — no positions) -> clone `letter_blank`. Clone = `action='get'` the starter, then `action='create'` with its html as your starting point. The starter already wires up the full STRUCTURE (regions, partials, data binding, translations) — do NOT re-derive it. (Tweaking an instance's EXISTING template instead? `get` that template and edit it — skip step 1.) STEP 2 — SKIN it: design the look ONLY in the template's `css` (it cascades after base.css and overrides every default). A new look = new css. Do NOT copy a fully-styled built-in's css — start from the starter's neutral skin and restyle. Set design tokens in `:root` (--fs-*, --col-*) first, then add per-region rules. STRUCTURE CONTRACT (what the starters give you — reference it, don't reinvent it): - Inherit the page frame: `{% extends "_base/base.html.j2" %}` (header/logo, @page margins, per-page footer boxes). Fill `{% block content %}`; override `{% block footer %}` only for a custom in-body footer. - Regions are
elements carrying `data-box=""` and a `.box-` class (base.css styles them; your css restyles them). Keys: recipient, info, subject, intro, items, totals, payment, notes, signature, shipping, contact-person, ship-to, body. - Reusable partials via `{% with ... %}{% include "_base/_partials/

.html.j2" %}{% endwith %}`: * items.html.j2 — positions table. Pass `items`, `labels=L`, `columns=[...]`. Column keys: pos|sku|article|qty|unit|unit_price|vat|total (order matters; the 6-col set matches base.css default widths). * recipient.html.j2 — address block. Pass `buyer`, `title`, optional `sender_line`. * totals.html.j2 — net / VAT-breakdown / gross. Pass `items`, `totals`, `labels=L`. * ship_to.html.j2, contact_person.html.j2 — optional blocks. - Text is `{{ L.key }}`; maintain strings with `set_translation` (per language), NOT an inline `_ALL_LANG` dict. The `L` map is injected from the template's translations at render time.

action.description: CRUD: list|get|render|create|update|delete. Targeted edits (validate-or-reject, change ONE thing without a full rewrite): list_blocks|get_block|set_block (one region, e.g. footer/items), set_style (font sizes / column-width tokens), set_asset (logo). Business config: set_translation (one language's UI strings), list_infoboxes|set_infobox|delete_infobox (placeable text blocks). Version history: list_versions (changelog, newest first), get_version (full snapshot of a `version`), restore_version (roll the template back to a `version`; the current state is saved as a new version first, so the restore is undoable).

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance. Required for all actions.

name.description: Template name (snake_case, 3-64 chars). Required for get/render/create/update/delete. For EXISTING templates the display title works too (exact, case-insensitive — e.g. 'Rechnung Acme v2'), so you don't have to guess a minted slug; ambiguous titles don't resolve. Structure starters to clone for NEW templates: `document_blank` (line-item documents) and `letter_blank` (free-form letters). Run `action='list'` to see all built-ins. Custom names must NOT collide with built-ins.

html.description: Jinja2 template body. Required for create. Begin with {% extends "_base/base.html.j2" %} and put the body in {% block content %}{% endblock %}.

css.description: Template CSS. base.css applies on top.

description.description: Public, human-readable description of what this template is for — shown in the template library/picker. Distinct from the two private free-text fields: `internal_comment` (why it was customised, onboarding rationale) and `note` (a per-version changelog line).

schema.description: Optional schema hint describing the data shape.

example_data.description: Realistic sample payload. The Documents editor uses this for previews. On a REAL document, only the keys listed in `global_fields` fall back from here — every other key is preview-only.

global_fields.description: For create/update: the top-level `example_data` keys that are ISSUER-GLOBAL — constant across every document the instance issues (e.g. ["company"]). ONLY these fall back into a REAL document when the live payload omits them; everything else in example_data is preview-only. Omit or pass [] = nothing falls back, so a build-time sample document number/date/recipient can never print on a customer's PDF.

compliance.description: Descriptive compliance tags — what the document claims to be, default ["pdf-ua-1"]. This is the SHORTHAND; its executable counterpart is `compliance_policy`. The tag→policy automatism: on create, an e-invoice format tag (e.g. "zugferd-en16931", "peppol") doesn't just label the template — it auto-derives and stores the real structured `compliance_policy` (PDF/A-3 + embedded XML). Pass `compliance_policy` to set/override that structured contract explicitly.

v3_endpoint.description: Optional Xentral V3 detail endpoint hint, e.g. "/api/v3/invoices/{id}?include=all".

languages.description: Languages the template ships (drives translations + the sidebar selector), e.g. ["de", "en"]. First = default.

data.description: Data dict passed to the renderer (action='render').

html_override.description: For action='render': override the saved html for a one-off preview.

css_override.description: For action='render': override the saved css.

fallback_to_example.description: For action='render': if true, deep-merge the template's ISSUER-GLOBAL example fields (`global_fields`) UNDER the provided data — fills instance-level constants (e.g. company info missing from a V3 response) without leaking per-document sample values. Mirrors the production render.

output.description:
For action='render':
- 'url' (DEFAULT, prefer this): saves the PDF server-side under an unguessable token and returns a short download_url. Hand the URL to the user — no large payload through the LLM context.
- 'metadata': returns only {filename, size_bytes} (useful for quick size check).
- 'base64': adds the full pdf_base64 inline. AVOID this — 50-150KB base64 streamed through the model context takes 30+ seconds and burns tokens. Only use when downstream tools strictly require the bytes inline.
- 'image': rasterizes the pages to PNG previews and returns one image_url per page (served as image/png). This is the ONLY output you can actually SEE — 'url' and 'base64' give you a PDF the model can't view. Use 'image' to VISUALLY verify the layout (orientation, columns, barcode sizes, overflow) after any change that affects optics, BEFORE reporting done.

internal_comment.description: Private onboarding rationale: WHY this PDF template was customised for the instance — set by the onboarding coach. One to three sentences: what business/branding signal drove the layout (CI colours, industry recipe, compliance regime). Shown on hover in the onboarding tab, never to the document recipient. Distinct from the public `description` (what the template is) and `note` (a per-version changelog line).

block.description: Block name for get_block/set_block — a region wrapped in <!-- box:NAME --> or a Jinja block. Standard: header, info, recipient, ship-to, items, totals, footer, contact.

tokens.description: For set_style: design-token → CSS value, e.g. {"fs-body": "11pt", "col-qty": "16mm"}. Tokens: fs-body, lh-body, fs-h1, fs-h2, fs-h3, fs-table, col-pos, col-qty, col-unit-price, col-vat, col-total.

asset_name.description: For set_asset: asset key, e.g. 'logo' (referenced as {{ assets.logo }}).

source.description: For set_asset: a data: URI or http(s) URL of the image.

lang.description: For set_translation: the language code (e.g. 'de', 'en') to merge strings into.

translations.description: For set_translation: {key: value} UI strings for `lang`, rendered as {{ L.key }}. Values may be strings, nested objects (L.sec.scope) or arrays of pairs (L.reasons).

infobox_key.description: For set_infobox/delete_infobox: the box's stable key/slug.

placement.description: For set_infobox: where the box renders. In-flow: intro_top, outro_bottom. Page margins: header_all/footer_all (every page), header_first/footer_first (page 1 only), header_rest/footer_rest (from page 2; WeasyPrint — Gotenberg shows on all pages). Absolute overlays (both engines): watermark (diagonal, centered) and stamp (corner, see `position`).

position.description: For set_infobox with placement='stamp': the corner preset (default top-right).

content.description: For set_infobox: {lang: text} body. May use Jinja, e.g. {{ data.iban }}.

enabled.description: For set_infobox: whether the box renders (default true).

intent.description: What the user is trying to produce, e.g. 'invoice'. Drives the DECISION flow only: for action='survey' it scopes the gap report; for action='create' it helps decide whether a clarification is needed. It does NOT persist anything — the stored doc-type binding is `document_type` (the template's templateId). Rule of thumb: `intent` steers the conversation, `document_type` is saved on the template.

locale.description: Response language for user-facing text: the help manual, survey notes and any needs_clarification prompt. 'en' (default) or 'de'. Does not affect keys, status or identifiers.

force.description: For action='create': skip the needs_clarification question (the soft readiness gate — e.g. when the e-invoice format for an invoice is still undecided) and create the template anyway. It bypasses ONLY that clarification prompt, not the required-field validation (name/title/html are still required).

note.description: Optional per-version changelog line — a short 'what changed and why' annotation for a version snapshot. Distinct from `description` (public, what the template is) and `internal_comment` (private onboarding rationale). Reserved: not yet persisted by the current actions.

analyze.description: For action='survey': also run a demand-side usage analysis (asks the Co-Pilot what the instance's real documents needed — languages, countries, currency — over the window) and attach a `usage` block. Slower (co-pilot round-trips); off by default.

window_months.description: For action='survey' with analyze=true: look-back window for the usage analysis in months (default 12, 1–60).

document_type.description: For action='create': the document type this template is for (invoice, delivery_note, sales_order, offer, credit_note, purchase_order, return). This is the PERSISTED binding — it sets the entity's templateId (distinct from `intent`, which only steers the survey/clarification flow and saves nothing). If omitted it is derived from name/v3_endpoint; pass it explicitly when the name is ambiguous so the template isn't stored under the generic default.

compliance_policy.description: For action='create'/'update': the STRUCTURED, executable e-invoice contract — `pdf_variant` (e.g. pdf/a-3b) + the embedded XML attachment — that actually makes an invoice an e-invoice (a `compliance` tag alone is only a label). This is the executable counterpart of the `compliance` tag list: on create you can omit it and pass the format in `compliance`, and the tag→policy automatism derives this for you; on update, supply it to add/replace the e-invoice policy on an existing template. `get` returns it back (attachment bodies elided to len+hash) so you can verify the config.

format_locale.description: For action='create'/'update': BCP-47 number/date format locale of the document (e.g. 'de-DE', 'de-CH', 'en-GB'). Drives the money/number/date filters. Distinct from `locale` (which is the en/de response language). Set it from the survey's derived locale_candidates.

scope.description: For action='create' (invoices): who the template is for — this_recipient (one named customer/supplier), customer_group, or all (default template). REQUIRED to pass the create gate for an invoice: it decides the evidence path (one recipient → read that record; group/all → run survey analyze=true and show the languages). Confirm it with the user, then pass it.

live.description: For action='check': also run a LIVE pass — render a REAL document and judge the actual output (ISO dates that should be localized, identifiers present in the data but missing from the page). If the template is an e-invoice (embedded-XML policy), it ALSO fetches that document's e-invoice XML from Xentral and validates it (EN 16931 / profile, malformed XML). Uses the most recent Beleg unless sample_doc_id is given. Slower (one render).

sample_doc_id.description: For action='check' with the live pass: the specific document id to render and inspect. Implies live=true; omit to use the most recent document for the template's v3_endpoint.

assets.description: For action='create'/'update': named inline images as {name: 'data:image/...;base64,...'}, referenced in the template as {{ assets.NAME }} (the letterhead uses assets.logo). The reliable way to ship a logo — get returns asset_names to confirm it stuck. On update this REPLACES the whole asset map; omit to keep stored.

engine.description: For action='create'/'update': render engine — 'gotenberg_chromium' (fast default) or 'weasyprint' (accessible/tagged PDF, reliable custom-font embedding). Omit to keep the current/default engine.

fields.description: For action='get': comma-separated allowlist to trim the response (e.g. 'html,css'). 'name' is always returned; assets always come back as asset_names (sizes), never raw data: URIs. To verify the e-invoice config, request 'compliance_policy' — get returns the executable policy (pdf_variant + attachment metadata, bodies elided to len+hash), distinct from the descriptive 'compliance' tag.

check_content.description: For action='check': also run the CONTENT-compliance layer — does the template bind the mandatory content for its document type (e.g. §14 UStG invoice fields) and the issuer's Geschäftsbrief disclosures? Off by default (advisory, not a gate). Implied when legal_form/industry is set.

legal_form.description: For action='check': issuer legal form (gmbh/ag/ohg_kg/ek) — drives the Geschäftsbrief mandatory-disclosure rules (§35a GmbHG / §80 AktG / §125a HGB / §37a HGB: register court + HRB, managing directors, …). Omit → GmbH assumed (a finding notes the assumption).

industry.description: For action='check': industry (food/electronics/pharma) — adds industry mandatory content (food → batch + best-before, electronics → serial numbers, pharma → batch + expiry).

tools.name: xentral_reports
tools.description:
Direct access to Xentral Analytics — SQL reports grouped into collections (folders), per instance. Use this when the user wants to explore, run or create analytics queries directly. For dashboard widgets that visualise a report, use `xentral_dashboards` instead.

Always discover with `list_collections` before drilling in.

Actions:
- `help` — full Markdown guide (collection model, parameter shapes, schema-budget, recipes). Pass `locale='de'`.
- `list_collections` — folders for the instance.
- `get_collection` — reports inside a collection.
- `get_report` / `run_report` — read or execute one report.
- `run_sql` — execute ad-hoc read-only SQL directly (no report is created); row count is capped upstream.
- `create_report` / `delete_report` — manage reports.
- `create_collection` — new folder.
- `get_schema` — data-model catalog (`table` filter recommended; raw dump is ~700 KB).

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for any action except `help`.

collection_id.description: Numeric collection id (folder). Required for `get_collection` and `create_report`.

title.description: Report title (create_report). Must be unique per instance.

sql_string.description: SQL statement (create_report, run_sql). SELECT/WITH only for `run_sql`; references declared parameters by name.

parameters.description: For `create_report` and `run_sql`: array of parameter declaration objects (Xentral schema, name/type/defaultValue). For `run_report`: flat object mapping declared parameter names to values.

table.description: Table label for `get_schema`. Omit to get the compact catalog of all tables; pass a label to get that table's full column list.

locale.description: UI locale, 'de' or 'en'. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_schedules
tools.description:
Cron schedules for the current license — list / create / update / delete plus an `audit` mode that joins the schedule service with its owning entities (agent slots, KPIs, dashboard widgets).

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown guide with cadence formats, audit semantics, recipes. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `list` — schedules for the instance (filterable by `category` / `enabled`).
- `create` — needs `category`, `resource_id`, `schedule={cadence, when, timezone?}`. See `help` for `when` formats per cadence (`daily` → `HH:mm`, `weekly` → `MON HH:mm`, …).
- `update` — change schedule by `id`; pass only fields you want to change.
- `delete` — idempotent.
- `audit` — find overdue / orphaned / missing / duplicate schedules. First call when a customer reports 'nothing is refreshing'.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance.

id.description: Schedule UUID. Required for update and delete.

category.description:
Entity type that owns the schedule. Required for create. Optional filter on list / audit.
- `xentral_agents`     — fires a custom-agent slot (resource_id = slot_id from xentral_agents action='custom_agent_list').
- `xentral_kpi`        — refreshes a KPI (resource_id = kpi_key).
- `xentral_dashboards` — refreshes a dashboard widget (resource_id = widget_id, or dashboard_slug for the whole dashboard).
DEPRECATED: `xentral_agent_jobs` is accepted as an alias for `xentral_agents`.

resource_id.description: Stable id of the owning entity: slot_id for agent jobs, kpi_key for KPIs, widget_id (or dashboard_slug for dashboard-wide) for dashboards. Required for create.

when.description: Format depends on cadence: 'HH:mm' (daily), 'MON HH:mm' (weekly), 'D. HH:mm' (monthly), 'Q1' (quarterly), 'DD.MM. HH:mm' (yearly), '<seconds>' (interval, minimum 60), 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' (appointment, one-shot).

timezone.description: IANA timezone. Defaults to Europe/Berlin. Persisted on the row so later license-TZ changes don't silently shift this schedule.

schedule.description: Required for create. Optional on update.

payload.description: Opaque dict copied 1:1 into the SQS message. Category-specific fields the worker expects (slot_id / kpi_key / dashboard_slug+widget_id).

enabled.description: Active flag. On create defaults to true. On update toggles pause/resume. Filter on list.

include_healthy.description: When true, `audit` also returns the OK rows with status='ok' (large output).

tools.name: xentral_shiplabel
tools.description:
Create carrier-agnostic shipping labels (DHL, DPD, UPS, FedEx, GLS, Sendcloud, Shipcloud, DHL Return). Build one canonical shipment request and get a tracking number plus a base64 label back, regardless of carrier. Carrier-direct — no Xentral instance involved.

Actions:
- `carriers` — list available carrier codes.
- `describe` — the request shape; with `carrier`, its config keys, supported services and output formats. Ask this first to learn what to pass.
- `create_label` — needs `request` (a canonical shipment request as JSON: `carrier.code`, `sender`, `recipient`, `parcels[]`), optionally `carrier` to override the code and `config` with the carrier credentials (else the backend env is used).

carrier.description: Carrier code (dhl, dpd, ups, fedex, gls, sendcloud, shipcloud, dhl_return). Overrides `request.carrier.code` when set; scopes `describe` to one carrier.

request.description: Canonical shipment request for `create_label`: `{carrier: {code, product}, sender, recipient, parcels: [{id, weight_kg, dimensions_cm}], references, label: {format}}`. Addresses need name/street/postal_code/city/country. `label.format` (pdf/zpl/png) is optional — omitted uses the carrier default.

config.description: Optional carrier credential keys (e.g. `dhl_api_key`, `dhl_username`, …). Merged over the backend env. Use for ad-hoc testing without setting SHIPLABEL_* env vars.

credential_ref.description: Reference to a stored credential-vault entry (planned). Not available yet — pass `config` inline for now.

include_label.description: Include the base64 label in the response (default true). Set false for a compact tracking-only reply.

tools.name: xentral_studio
tools.description:
Instance-scoped Studio app store. A Studio App is a composed surface — your own screens and components (forms, tables, buttons) on top of the global Business-Entity catalogue, running as a Mobile or Desktop app. Apps are persisted per instance, exactly like Dashboards and Agents.

Use Studio when the user needs a custom operational screen the standard ERP UI doesn't offer (a warehouse scan view, a field-sales order pad, a commission-run desk). For automated step sequences use `xentral_workflows`; for content-dependent decisions use `xentral_agents`.

ALWAYS call `help` first when building an app — it returns the full app/screen/component schema, the component-type catalogue and the valid `linked_entities`. Pass `locale='de'` for German.

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual (app anatomy, component types, examples). Read this before authoring.
- `list_library` — built-in app templates (bestellvorschlag, lager, pick, aussendienst, provisionsabrechnung).
- `get_library` — one template's full payload. Requires `template_id` (the template slug).
- `list_entities` — the global Business-Entity catalogue an app may reference via `linked_entities`.
- `list` — all custom apps of the instance.
- `get` — full payload for one app. Requires `slug`.
- `create` — either clone a template (pass `template_id`) or build a blank/custom app directly (pass `slug` + `name`, plus `form`, `platform`, `linked_entities`, …). New apps start as drafts (`enabled=false`).
- `update` — patch semantics; only passed fields overwrite. Requires `slug`.
- `set_enabled` — activate/deactivate an app. Requires `slug` and `enabled`.
- `link` — return the public preview URL for the app (the same token link the designer's QR uses). Requires `slug`. Render it as a QR so it opens on a phone; sign the device into the instance for live data and executable buttons.
- `delete` — hard-delete a custom app. Requires `slug`.
- `compose_ui` — natural-language screen authoring. Pass `slug` and `request` (one complete instruction, in the user's language). A validated composer rewrites the app's screens (dropping any hallucinated component/binding) and persists them. PREFER this over hand-writing `form` JSON when editing the open app — the user's IDE refreshes automatically.
- `write_file` / `delete_file` — edit one Python code file of the app. Requires `slug` + `path` (+ `content`, `lang` for write).
- `upsert_tool` / `delete_tool` — create/update/remove one MCP tool of the app (callable from buttons via `tool:<name>`). Requires `slug` + `tool_name` (+ `tool_description`, `params`, `entrypoint` for upsert). `entrypoint` is the path of an existing code file.

AUTHORING CONTRACT: your job is the app DEFINITION — the screen/component tree and which global entities it binds to. The `form.screens[].components[]` tree is what renders. Wire buttons that NAVIGATE with `props.action` = `screen:<id>` | `dialog:<id>`. Wire buttons that DO something with `props.binding` = { kind:'steps', steps:[…] } — an entity `action` (mark picked, print Paketmarke), a `workflow` step (shared webhook, get its `shareId` from `xentral_workflows` share), `setfields`, or `api`. `props.action='tool:<name>'` only shows a toast (no execution) — prefer `binding`. When editing the OPEN app (focus `entity_type=studio_app`), use `compose_ui` for UI and `write_file`/`upsert_tool` for logic — do not re-send the whole `form`. `slug` is snake_case (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{2,127}$), unique per instance, and must not collide with a built-in template slug. Validation is advisory; writes are never blocked (same as the designer UI).

tools.name: xentral_user_context
tools.description:
Read where the user is currently looking in the Xentral app, or push a UI command to their browser via the live SSE channel.

Use this BEFORE other tools when the user's request is location-dependent — e.g. 'open the customer I'm on', 'show me the letterhead', 'create a return for this order'. The context tells you which entity_id / entity_type to act on without having to ask the user.

Actions:
- `get_context` — return the user's current page, route, and active entity. Cheap to call. Returns 'no active focus' when the user is not in the app or their session has expired (120 s TTL after the last frontend heartbeat).
- `set_view` — switch the app to a top-level overview page. Requires `view`. Use this ONLY for 'geh zur Agenten-Übersicht', 'open the Dashboards overview', etc. When the user names a specific item ('öffne X', 'gehe in X', 'X bearbeiten', etc.), use `open_entity` INSTEAD — the optional `entity_id` parameter on `set_view` only scrolls/highlights the card, it does NOT open the editor. Pass the id exactly — shortened keys land in a generic fallback. Known views: `dashboard` (cockpit), `jobs`, `groups`, `learning-loop`, `decisions-admin`, `business-model`, `onboarding`, `agents-overview`, `workflows-overview`, `dashboards`, `kpis`, `integrations-hub`, `templates`, `schedules`, `files`, `business-entities`, `studio` (Studio app overview), `marketplace`, `settings`, `create-agent`, `create-workflow`, plus the workspace tables `workspace-customers`, `workspace-suppliers`, `workspace-returns`, `workspace-products`, `workspace-purchase-orders`, `workspace-inbox`, `workspace-procurement-inbox`, and individual dashboards via `workspace-dashboard-<slug>`. Optional `entity_id` highlights/scrolls to a specific item once mounted.
- `open_entity` — open a SPECIFIC item by type + id. Requires `entity_type` and `entity_id`. Use this for 'öffne den Workflow X', 'show me KPI Y', etc.
  MANDATORY SEQUENCE for any 'öffne X' request — execute in this exact order, never skip step 3:
    1. Call `xentral_inventory` action=`list` if you don't already know `entity_type` + `entity_id`.
    2. Fuzzy-match the user's name against the items.
    3. CALL `open_entity` with the matched pair. This is the step that actually opens the page. The tool returns a confirmation; only after seeing 'Done — open_entity … pushed' may you tell the user it's open.
    4. If the tool returns 'no app tab open' or '0 subscribers', say so plainly — never claim success.
  NEVER respond with 'X ist offen' / 'X is open' without having actually called `open_entity` in this same turn. Types: URL-routed (`sales_order`, `customer`, `product`, `invoice`, `return`), document (`pdf_template`, `letterhead`), and workspace items that each open their editor inside the matching overview (`workflow` → wf.id; `dashboard` → slug; `kpi` → key; `custom_agent` → agent_name incl. `slot:` prefix; `integration` → id like 'shopify', 'slack', 'dhl'; `studio_app` → app slug (opens the Studio app IDE); `job` → job id; `business_model_section` → section slug).
- `navigate` — open a literal `/app/...` URL. Almost never needed — prefer `set_view` or `open_entity`. The route MUST start with `/app/`; anything else is rejected by the frontend (non-`/app/` paths bounce the user to the public landing page).
- `show_toast` — non-modal hint at top of screen. Requires `message`; optional `level` (info|success|warn|error).

When a push action reports 0 subscribers, the user does not have the app open in any tab — your action was a no-op. Tell them to open it or fall back to plain text.

route.description: For `navigate`: a frontend route. MUST start with `/app/` (e.g. '/app/jobs/12345', '/app/sales/SO-100'). Anything else is rejected to prevent kicking the user to the marketing landing page. For overviews use `set_view`, for entities use `open_entity` — `navigate` is only for explicit URL deep-links.

entity_type.description: For `open_entity`: one of 'sales_order', 'customer', 'product', 'invoice', 'return', 'pdf_template' (custom PDF templates — invoice, delivery note, offer, etc.), 'letterhead' (per-instance letterhead singleton only), 'custom_agent' (pass agent_name, e.g. 'slot:abc123' for schedule slots), 'workflow' (pass wf.id), 'dashboard' (pass slug), 'kpi' (pass key, e.g. 'sales_orders_open_count'), 'integration' (pass id, e.g. 'shopify', 'slack', 'dhl'), 'job', 'business_model_section'. PDF templates created by the user are `pdf_template`, NOT `letterhead`.

entity_id.description: For `open_entity`: the external id of the entity (e.g. 'SO-12345'). For `set_view`: optional id to highlight/scroll to once the view mounts.

view.description: For `set_view`: a top-level view id, e.g. 'agents-overview' (Agenten), 'workflows-overview' (Workflows), 'dashboards', 'kpis', 'integrations' (Connections), 'templates' (PDF Templates), 'schedules' (Zeitplan), 'business-model', 'dashboard' (cockpit), or a custom agent's id. See the full list in the tool description — use the exact id, do not abbreviate.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

tools.name: xentral_workflow_debug
tools.description: Debug a designer workflow hands-on, like an engineer with API access. START with `runs` when the complaint is that a workflow did not do its job: it lists what the workflow ACTUALLY did in the last 24h, and `trace` opens one run down to the node that failed. An unattended workflow that never fired and one that fired and failed look identical from the graph — only this tells them apart, so read it before theorising about triggers or subscriptions. Then: read the definition (`overview`) and its compiled Python (`python`), test hypotheses against the live Xentral API with throwaway Python probes in the workflow sandbox (`run_script`, which runs behind the same runtime prelude a workflow gets, so `business_entity_op` / `xentral_request` resolve exactly as they do in a Code node and a probe finding transfers to the graph), test ONE node in isolation against the live instance (`run_node`) — the cheapest way to confirm a read/source node's endpoint resolves and returns the expected data before running the whole graph — reproduce failures with a real run (`run_workflow`), then FIX the workflow yourself via `apply_patch` and verify — don't hand the user a manual edit. Call action='help' FIRST for the working loop, the script environment (auth env vars, page[size] trap, id-vs-uuid trap) and the patch format. To exercise a write workflow safely, pass `dry_run=True` to `run_workflow`/`run_node`: the graph runs but every mutating call is suppressed and logged instead of performed, with a structured node/method/entity/id/body trace. Use `test_scenarios` for deterministic fixtures: every Business Entity read must have an `Entity:id` or `Entity:list` fixture, all other live reads are blocked, and `expect.writes` is compared one-to-one with the suppressed writes. To test a workflow whose input comes from the caller (webhook / integration-event triggers), pass `trigger_payload` — the live trigger envelope (a webhook delivers `{method, query, headers, body}`, so a POST body reads as `{{ trigger.body.x }}`); without it `{{ trigger.* }}` is empty and the run is not representative. Warning to surface to the user before the first side-effecting step: a REAL `run_workflow`/`run_node` (dry_run off) executes real emails/ERP writes and `apply_patch` edits the saved workflow — recommend full auto-debugging only on sandbox/test instances.

instance_id.description: License ID of the Xentral instance.

workflow_id.description: Workflow id (from xentral_workflows list/get) — required for overview/python/run_node/run_workflow/apply_patch. Optional for `runs`: omit it to see every run on the instance, which is how you find out whether an event arrived at all.

trace_id.description: For `trace` (required): the id of one run, taken from a `runs` row.

limit.description: For `runs` (optional): how many runs to return, newest first. Default 20.

node_id.description: For run_node: id of the single node to execute (see `overview` for node ids).

op_id.description: For run_node: override the operation a resource node runs (e.g. 'list'/'read'/'create'). Default: taken from the saved graph's incoming edge.

ctx_seed.description: For run_node: pre-populate `context` so the node's upstream `{{ }}` refs resolve without running upstream boxes — keys are upstream node var names, values their sample outputs.

trigger_payload.description: For run_workflow/run_node: the run's input, so a workflow whose input comes from the CALLER (webhook / integration-event triggers, not an ERP read) can be tested with realistic data — without it `{{ trigger.* }}` is empty. Pass the live trigger envelope: a webhook delivers `{"method", "query", "headers", "body"}`, so a POST body `{"name":"Ada"}` reads as `{{ trigger.body.name }}`. (ctx_seed cannot seed this — main() overwrites the trigger namespace.)

trigger_kind.description: For run_workflow: which START node the simulated run comes in through. Only matters for a workflow that carries several starts (a workflow may hold one start of each kind, all wired into the same first step) — without it every start box lights up in the transcript, with it only the named one does. The flow itself runs the same either way.

dry_run.description: For run_workflow/run_node: run the graph but SUPPRESS every mutating HTTP call (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) — writes to Xentral, the entity gateway, jobs/tasks and email return a synthetic 200 and are logged as `[dry-run] suppressed …`. Reads (GET) still run live. Use to exercise a write workflow end-to-end with zero side effects. Default false.

structured.description: For run_workflow with dry_run=true: return JSON with canonical suppressed writes ({node, method, entity, id, operation, body}) instead of a text transcript. Cannot be used for a real run.

scenarios.description: For test_scenarios: deterministic cases; omit to use the saved workflow's build_contract.tests. Each item is {name, trigger_payload?, trigger_kind?, fixtures, expect:{writes}}. Fixture keys are 'Entity:id' for read and 'Entity:list' for list. Expected writes are subset-shaped objects matched one-to-one, e.g. {entity:'SalesOrder', id:'42', operation:'update', body:{...}}; use writes:[] to assert no side effects. Missing fixtures never fall back to live ERP reads. Max 20 cases / 128 KB fixtures each.

script.description: Python source for run_script (see action='help' for the environment).

runtime_profile.description: Sandbox envelope for run_script (~60s vs ~300s). Default small.

changes.description: For apply_patch: [{node_id, config_key, new_value}, …]. new_value may contain {{ }} bindings.

locale.description: Guide language for action='help'. Defaults to 'en'.

tools.name: xentral_workflows
tools.description:
Instance-scoped workflow store. Each workflow is a directed graph: a trigger fires, then action nodes execute in the order defined by the edges. A workflow may carry SEVERAL start nodes so one flow is reachable more than one way (manual + schedule + ERP event), under two rules: at most one start of each kind, and every start wired into the same first step — the flow is emitted once and shared, only the start that fired runs. Breaking either is reported as `duplicate_trigger_kind` or `trigger_flows_diverge`. Workflows are explicit step lists — deterministic, idempotent, ideal for routine operations (dunning, prepayment cleanup, return-to-credit-note, low-stock reordering). Structured content-dependent decisions belong in deterministic condition/loop/entity nodes; use `xentral_agents` only for genuinely unstructured reasoning.

Lifecycle: `init` (or `init_from_template`) registers a new workflow once. `update` merges patch-style changes. `delete` hard-removes the envelope and index entry.

The workflow library ships several ERP-classic templates (prepayment cancellation, dunning escalation, return → credit note, daily OPOS digest, auto-release paid orders, low-stock reorder proposal, invoice after shipment). Use `list_library` to discover them and `init_from_template` to clone one into the instance.

Actions:
- `help` — Markdown manual. Pass `locale='de'` for German.
- `list` — slim overview of every workflow (id, name, description, trigger_type, enabled, scheduled, node/edge counts, timestamps), newest first. Does NOT include the graph — call `get` for the full nodes/edges of a specific workflow.
- `get` — full envelope for one workflow. Requires `id`.
- `preflight` — read-only capability check for `build_contract` against the authenticated tenant's active core; reads metadata/events only.
- `validate` — read-only verdict on a graph's well-formedness and buildability. Pass `nodes` (+optional `edges`, `trigger_type`) to pre-flight a graph before `init`, or `id` to check a stored workflow. Returns `{valid, errors, warnings, checked}`. `init`/`init_from_template`/`update` also attach this report under `validation`. Most findings are advisory, but a write is REJECTED (nothing saved) when the payload can never render or run: an unknown node `typeId`, or an edge wired out of a terminal node (`output`, `human-task`) / into a trigger or note. The error lists what to fix — correct the payload and resend.
- `check` — read-only post-build health check, similar to the PDF-template check: runs `validate` plus agent-learned workflow hygiene rules (visible business-entity/fileshare modelling, operation handle integrity, anti-code/xentral-action warnings, printer/file binding checks, and whether a dry-run is recommended). It does NOT execute the workflow; use `xentral_workflow_debug` for node probes or dry-runs.
- `init` — create a new workflow. Requires `id`, `name`. Optional `description`, `trigger_type`, `nodes`, `edges`, `enabled`, `orientation`. Duplicate id → 409-style error.
- `init_from_template` — clone a library template into the instance. Requires `id` (new workflow id, unique per instance) and `template_id`. Optional overrides for `name`, `description`, `trigger_type`, `nodes`, `edges`, `enabled`.
- `update` — patch semantics. Only passed fields overwrite. `id` and `created_at` are protected.
- `delete` — hard-delete envelope + index entry.
- `share` — manage the public webhook Share (requires `id`). `share_op`: `get` (current share + public_url), `save` (create/activate, optional `share_token`, `share_active`), `rotate` (new share_id, old URL dies), `delete`. This is what makes a `trigger-webhook` workflow callable at `/wh/{share_id}`.
- `erp_event` — manage the Xentral subscription behind a `trigger-erp-event` workflow (requires `id`). `erp_event_op`: `get`, `activate` (needs `event`), `deactivate`. REQUIRED after building an `in-erp` workflow: saving the graph does not subscribe anything, so without `activate` Xentral pushes no events and the workflow never fires — while `validate` and `check` still look clean.
- `list_library` — list shippable ERP-classic templates, localised to the requested `locale`.
- `get_library` — one library template, localised. Requires `template_id`.

CALLING A WORKFLOW VIA API (webhook request/response):
A `trigger-webhook` workflow is a request→response endpoint. Shape it as trigger → processing → an `output` node (terminal; `config.value` is a template field that becomes the return value). The incoming request reaches the graph as a fixed envelope: the POST body is `{{ trigger.body.<field> }}` (NOT flat `{{ trigger.<field> }}`), plus `{{ trigger.query.<key> }}`, `{{ trigger.headers.<key> }}`, `{{ trigger.method }}`. The workflow only becomes reachable once a Share (share_id + optional token) is minted — mint it here with `action='share', share_op='save'` (returns the `public_url`), or in the designer's webhook inspector. Callers then `POST /wh/{share_id}?token=…`: with `?wait=1` the call is synchronous and returns `{status, run_id, output}` (the `output` node's value); without it the call returns `202 {accepted, run_id}` immediately (fire-and-forget). Because the input comes from the caller, test such a workflow with `xentral_workflow_debug.run_workflow(trigger_payload=…)`, not the ERP-read probe loop.

AUTHORING CONTRACT (read before you build a workflow):
Your job is the workflow GRAPH — pick the right node types and wire their input/output ports correctly. Code is allowed for genuine program logic, but not as an escape hatch for unclear modelling. Fixed ERP reads/writes and business decisions belong on the canvas. A Code node may contain complex calculations, data reshaping, aggregation, dynamic traversal, or glue code over visible upstream data. Every Code node MUST include `config.description` written for a CEO/business owner, not for a developer: start with the business purpose, state what data comes in, what decision or reshaping happens, and what the next step receives. Avoid API/Python terms and raw field names in prose; when a field matters, name the business meaning first and put the technical field in parentheses only when useful. Non-trivial Code MUST include `config.algorithm` with 3-6 business steps or a small ASCII sketch, not implementation details. Python comments inside Code nodes MUST be in English and explain important loops, branches, aggregations, reshaping or side effects. If the logic would only be possible as an opaque Code box, stop and name the missing prerequisite instead: missing Business Entity field, missing action, missing transform/filter node, missing runtime probe, or missing business rule.

NODE-TYPE PRIORITY (compose with deterministic primitives first; `agent` and `code` are last resorts):
Use the deterministic native node types BEFORE reaching for an `agent` (LLM step) or `code` (Python) node. The deterministic primitives keep the graph readable in the designer, are cheap and predictable at runtime, give the engine introspection (per-step status, retries, replay), and don't depend on someone else writing Python afterwards. Default order:
  1. `business-entity` (list/read/create/update/delete on a Xentral entity) for any ERP read or write — including filtered list retrieval, single-record lookup, and updates by id. List enumeration is THIS node, not an agent. Its OUTPUT IS THE RECORD as `describe` shows it — a list for `list`: loop over `{{ orders }}`, read `{{ order.id }}`, bind `path: "id"`, and in a Code box `order['items']`. It used to hand back a `{status, headers, body}` hull; a reference still written as `{{ order.body.data.x }}` resolves to nothing and the step runs green on empty data, so it is rejected as `entity_ref_uses_stale_envelope`.
  2. `condition` for yes/no branches — expression goes in the config, two outgoing edges via `sourceHandle: a|b` (a = Yes, b = No — "yes"/"no" are rejected).
  3. `loop` for for-each over a list — anything per-item downstream attaches to the loop's output.
  4. `integration-action` for ANY third-party service the instance integrates with (shop / marketplace / CRM / mail / messaging — e.g. Shopify, HubSpot, Slack): it runs one action of that integration via the provider-neutral connector registry. Author it EVEN WHEN the integration is not connected yet (provisional node, empty `connection_id`) — NEVER fall back to an `http-request` against the vendor's REST API for a service that has an integration.
  5. `shiplabel` for a carrier / parcel label (DHL, DPD, UPS, GLS, …) — the ONE way to create a shipping label in a workflow. Never model a carrier label as `http-request`, a `business-entity` action, `xentral-api` or `code`; there is no shipping-label ERP action.
  6. `http-request`, `delay`, `web-search` for the specialised remaining cases. `http-request` is a RAW escape hatch for a plain REST endpoint with NO integration behind it — it is NOT the way to talk to Shopify or any known SaaS (use `integration-action`), and NEVER a way to reach Xentral.
  NOT AVAILABLE: `xentral-api`, and `xentral_request` / `xentral_op` / `xentral_action` / bare `requests` inside a Code box. Every Xentral read and write goes through the entity core, so a graph carrying one is reported as `raw_erp_access_forbidden`. When the core cannot express what you need, say so and STOP — the gap is reported automatically so the core can gain the capability, which is the fix that also helps the next tenant. Routing around it produces a workflow that looks finished and quietly does the wrong thing.
  7. `agent` ONLY when the step genuinely needs natural-language reasoning that no deterministic primitive can express: free-text classification, intent detection in customer prose, ambiguous extraction from an unstructured email body, drafting a reply. Filtering structured Xentral data, picking records that match a rule, computing a threshold, mapping fields between entities — NONE of these are agent jobs; they are `business-entity` + `condition` + `loop`.
  8. `code` ONLY when (a) the data transform genuinely doesn't fit a chain of the above, or (b) the topology is not a flat DAG of the native primitives (recursion, dynamic graph shape, intricate aggregation across loop iterations). Even then it must stay reviewable: max 500 non-empty lines, no semicolon compression, clear helper function names, English comments for important sections, and no fixed ERP reads/writes hidden inside code.
Recognising the boundary is a judgment call — if a designer-user could draw the flow as condition + loop + entity nodes, that is the correct implementation, even if an agent or single code-node would be shorter JSON.
Anti-patterns: (i) collapsing the whole workflow into one big `code` node because it's faster to write; (ii) using an `agent` step to "figure out" which records to act on when an entity-list + condition would do the same job deterministically. The graph must stay legible to a non-technical user opening the canvas.

MCP BUILD LOOP:
Before building, express ERP dependencies in `build_contract` and call `preflight`; discover the available template, entity, field, action and process-step surface; do not guess. A failed preflight may be saved only as a disabled draft. Add contract fixture tests for at least the positive write case and every important no-write branch; enabled writes auto-run these tests. After every `init` or `update`, run `check`. Treat errors as not done, fix the graph, and check again; for reachable writes use or recommend `xentral_workflow_debug.run_workflow(dry_run=true)` before a real run. If you get stuck, distinguish local instance issues from generic platform gaps. Do NOT report one-off issues such as missing instance data, missing mail account, or an absent tag as product feedback. If the workflow would be cleanly buildable only with a generally useful missing Business Skill — e.g. a central Business Entity field, an ERP action exposed as an entity action, a standard transform/filter/aggregation node, or a new check rule — record that via `xentral_feedback` with `category='feature_request'` or `category='bug'` and `request_report=true`. Keep the feedback general and avoid customer/document/email contents. Then tell the user the workflow is blocked by that missing general capability instead of hiding the gap inside a complex Code node.

TITLES & DESCRIPTION (mandatory, business-readable):
Every node gets a `config.title` written for a business reader — a CEO must be able to follow the flow from the titles alone. Actions: verb + object ('Load all products from Xentral', 'Cancel the unpaid order'). Conditions: a full question ('Is the product a bill of materials?'). Loops: 'For each <item>: <purpose>'. Never identifier-style titles like `pid` or `ekObjekt`. Nodes referenced via `{{ }}` or in expressions additionally pin their identifier with `config.varName` (short camelCase, e.g. `openOrders`) so retitling never breaks references. The workflow `description` is markdown and must explain — so a business reader understands it without opening the canvas — what the workflow does (plain opening paragraph, no markup; it doubles as the card teaser), how the algorithm works (optionally a small ASCII flow sketch in a ``` fence for branch/loop/recursion shapes), what happens step by step (numbered list mirroring the node titles), what it changes in Xentral (bullets; name every write or state that nothing is changed), and its prerequisites/limits (bullets). Bold section headings, not `#`.

instance_id.description: License ID of the instance. Required for instance-scoped actions.

id.description: Workflow id (snake_case, 3-64 chars). Generated by the caller.

name.description: Human-readable workflow name shown in the designer.

description.description: Short description of what the workflow does.

nodes.description: React-Flow nodes. Each node has `id`, `type='wfNode'`, `position`, and `data: { typeId, config }`. See `help` for the available `typeId` values.

orientation.description: Canvas reading direction. Prefer 'horizontal' for new workflows unless the user asks otherwise or a long checklist/runbook is clearly easier top-to-bottom. 'horizontal' = left → right; keep y constant and grow x by about 400 per step. 'vertical' = top → bottom; keep x constant and space y by card height.

template_id.description: ID of a library template, e.g. 'prepayment_order_cleanup', 'opos_dunning_escalation', 'return_to_credit_note'. Use `list_library` to enumerate.

share_op.description: For action='share' (requires `id`): manage the public webhook Share that makes a `trigger-webhook` workflow callable at `/wh/{share_id}`. `get` returns the current share + public_url (or null); `save` creates/activates it (optionally gated by `share_token`); `rotate` mints a new share_id (old URL dies); `delete` removes it. Default `get`.

share_token.description: For action='share', share_op='save': optional secret required as `?token=` on the public endpoint. Omit/empty → reachable by link alone.

share_active.description: For action='share', share_op='save': activation gate. Default true. Set false to configure a share that stays 404 until flipped live.

erp_event_op.description: For action='erp_event' (requires `id`): manage the Xentral webhook subscription behind a `trigger-erp-event` workflow. Building the graph alone does NOT subscribe anything — until `activate` runs, Xentral pushes no events and the workflow never fires. `get` reports the current state; `activate` (needs `event`) registers at Xentral; `deactivate` removes the subscription. Default `get`.

event.description: For action='erp_event', erp_event_op='activate': the event-type id in the active ERP core's own vocabulary — for Xentral e.g. 'com.xentral.salesOrder.created.v1'. Enumerate the valid ids with `xentral_erp_core action='events'` — the catalogue is a core capability and lives there; this tool only subscribes one of them. The ids are per-installation and per-version, so never guess: an unknown id is refused at activation.

core_id.description: For action='erp_event': which of the instance's ACTIVATED cores to register the webhook against, and whose event catalogue applies. Omit for the primary. Only matters when several cores are active and do not share an event source — e.g. a non-Xentral primary with an activated Xentral secondary, where the primary alone reports that events are impossible. Ids come from xentral_erp_core action='list'.

connection_id.description: For action='erp_event', erp_event_op='activate': which ERP connection to subscribe through. Omit for the tenant's default. Recorded on the subscription so a later teardown targets the same system.

verify.description: For init/init_from_template/update: after saving, dry-run the workflow once (writes suppressed, reads live on this instance) to confirm it actually does something — catching the 'green run that does nothing' (empty loop, wrong ref) the static validator can't see. Default on when the static check is clean; set false to skip (e.g. while still assembling the graph).

build_contract.description: Optional machine-checkable authoring contract. New contracts use version:2 (which requires fixture tests): trigger plus requirements.reads/writes/relations, rules and effects. Requirement shape: {entity, operation, fields:[dotted paths]}; relation shape: {from:'Entity.path', to:'Entity.path'}; rule shape: {id,nodeId}; effect shape: {when:[rule ids], update:{entity,operation}}. Use tests:[{name,trigger_payload?,fixtures,expect:{writes}}] with synthetic/anonymized values to persist the deterministic PR4 scenarios consumed by xentral_workflow_debug action='test_scenarios'. Use action='preflight' before building. When present, check verifies graph coverage and enabled writes are rejected while capability blockers remain.

locale.description: UI locale for `help`, `list_library`, `get_library`. Unknown values fall back to 'en'.
